_comment: Authored analysis: ownership, lifecycle, refcount and locking judgements that no composer can derive, keyed to the C entities they describe. The structural half of each record (field layout, signatures, footprints, casts) is composed from the CodeQL tables on demand and merged in at read time, so a re-extract rewrites nothing here. Written only by `wavefront <repo> <target> query {types,symbols} --update`; read through wavefront.manifests. Hand-edit at your own risk: `--update` validates a submission against the composed skeleton (unknown field, wrong kind, ptr-invariant violation) and this file does not.

types.name: git_allocator
types._comment_agent: A plain vtable value: no lifecycle of its own. git_allocator_setup (GIT_OPT_SET_ALLOCATOR) memcpys the caller's struct into the hidden global git__allocator, so the caller's storage is borrowed for the call only. The init routines git_stdalloc_init_allocator / git_debugalloc_init_allocator fill caller storage but are not exported from libgit2.so (declared without GIT_EXTERN, hidden), and git_win32_crtdbg_init_allocator is declared but never defined on this build; the only public producer is a value the caller fills itself. The three members form one allocator family: storage from gmalloc/grealloc must be released by the same family's grealloc/gfree, and libgit2 calls them from any thread.

ptr.note: Function pointer to code: static. Releases a live allocation of this allocator; NULL is a no-op. Called unconditionally by git__free, so it must be set when installed.

Function pointer to code: static, never owned or freed. libgit2 calls it unconditionally through git__allocator (git__malloc, threadstate_get), so every installed allocator must set it (git2/sys/alloc.h: 'all fields need to be set'); the C type admits NULL (bindgen Option), which only a never-installed value may hold. Returns fresh storage of >= n bytes or NULL; file/line are the call site (__FILE__, a static string) and are borrowed for the call.

Function pointer to code: static. C realloc contract: consumes a live allocation of this allocator (or NULL = malloc) and returns a new one of `size` bytes, or NULL leaving the old one live. Called unconditionally by git__realloc / git__reallocarray, so it must be set when installed.

types.name: git_annotated_commit
types._comment_agent: Opaque in the public API (forward-declared in include/git2/types.h); built only by annotated_commit.c's constructors (REAL: git__calloc + git_commit_dup + git__strdup) and merge.c's create_virtual_base (VIRTUAL: index + parents), released only by git_annotated_commit_free, which switches on `type` (REAL frees commit, tree, description, ref_name, remote_url; VIRTUAL frees index and the parents array; anything else aborts). No dup/clone routine exists. merge.c casts `const git_annotated_commit **` heads to mutable and lazily caches `tree` (annotated_commit_tree), so a const pointer does not mean read-only. The embedded commit is a counted reference into the repository's object cache (atomic refcount); freeing it never touches the repository.

ptr.note: REAL only: a counted reference taken by git_commit_dup (git_cached_obj refcount, atomic), released by git_commit_free in git_annotated_commit_free; NULL for VIRTUAL. Read by git_annotated_commit_id (git_commit_id), reset.c, branch.c, merge.c.

REAL: git__strdup of the lookup description (revspec, reference name, fetchhead branch name, or id_str); never NULL after a successful constructor (strdup failure leaks the half-built object and returns -1 with *out NULL). Freed with git__free. NULL for VIRTUAL. Read by reset.c and branch.c as reflog messages.
VIRTUAL only (create_virtual_base adopts the merged index); read by iterator_for_annotated_commit; freed by git_index_free in the VIRTUAL branch. NULL for REAL.

git__strdup of the reference name (from_ref, from_head) or branch name (from_fetchhead); NULL for lookup/from_revspec/VIRTUAL, and NULL when that strdup fails (constructor returns -1 but leaves *out set). git__free'd. Returned borrowed by git_annotated_commit_ref.
from_fetchhead only: git__strdup of remote_url; NULL otherwise, and NULL when that strdup fails (constructor returns -1 but leaves *out set). git__free'd; read by merge_msg_write_remotes.

NULL after every public constructor; merge.c's annotated_commit_tree fills it lazily (git_commit_tree) through a casted const head and hands out git_tree_dup copies; freed by git_tree_free in the REAL branch of git_annotated_commit_free.

types.name: git_branch_t
types._comment_agent: core wave 0 batch 0 (2026-10-09). Flag-shaped enum: LOCAL = 1, REMOTE = 2, ALL = LOCAL|REMOTE. git_branch_iterator_new stores it as unsigned flags and git_branch_next tests each bit (0 lists nothing, extra bits are ignored) and writes only LOCAL or REMOTE to *out_type; git_branch_lookup switches on it and hits GIT_ASSERT(false) for any other value (-1 'unrecoverable internal error' in release, abort in the Debug/coverage build). Wrapped as the closed Rust enum BranchType, so the asserting values are unrepresentable.

types.name: git_buf
types._comment_agent: core wave 0 batch 0 (2026-10-09). Wrapped as Buf / BufRef / BufMut, owned by value as BufVal = CVal<Buf, BufDispose>; the safe API keeps the invariant 'reserved == 0 owns nothing and reads empty; reserved > 0 owns a libgit2-allocator buffer with size < reserved and ptr[size] == NUL'. BufDispose calls git_buf_dispose only when reserved > 0. Review (core review wave 0, 2026-10-09): Buf::from_raw's contract now also requires ptr[0..size) initialised and exclusive while the owner lives; git_repository_discover is the one public filler that skips git_buf_tostr.

ptr.note: A byte buffer of `size` bytes, NUL-terminated at ptr[size] (contents may hold interior NULs: diff/patch/pack output). Ownership is runtime-conditional: libgit2's producers (git_buf_fromstr) leave reserved = git_str asize, so reserved > 0 means ptr is a git__malloc buffer of >= reserved bytes the struct owns, writable and reusable (git_buf_sanitize writes ptr[0], git_buf_tostr adopts it as git_str asize and may git__realloc it). reserved == 0 means it owns nothing: ptr is NULL (GIT_BUF_INIT) or the hidden static git_str__initstr (size 0), which git_buf_tostr/sanitize replace without freeing. git_buf_dispose itself frees any ptr != git_str__initstr (git__free(NULL) for GIT_BUF_INIT, which reads git__allocator unsynchronised against a first git_libgit2_init), so a reserved == 0 buffer with a foreign non-NULL ptr would be freed by dispose yet dropped by sanitize. The one producer of that shape is the internal git_merge_driver__builtin_apply (merged_out reserved = 0 over an owned, non-NUL-terminated merge result, disposed by merge_conflict_invoke_driver); no public routine hands it out. The header's 'reserved and unused' comment is wrong. Every public producer first passes the caller's struct through git_buf_tostr (reusing or git__realloc-ing a reserved > 0 allocation, or dropping a reserved == 0 ptr) except git_repository_discover, which writes `out` with git_buf_fromstr(out, &paths.gitdir) directly: a reserved > 0 allocation handed in is overwritten and LEAKED (no use-after-free: fromstr moves the git_str out before repo_paths_dispose). Its wrapper must fill a fresh Buf::new(), as the convention already says (core review wave 0, 2026-10-09).

types.name: git_buildinfo_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless enum, passed by value only; no pointer, no lifecycle (core wave 0 batch 1, 2026-10-09). Sole consumer git_libgit2_buildinfo (settings.c:478) switches on it: GIT_BUILDINFO_CPU (1) returns the static string GIT_BUILD_CPU, GIT_BUILDINFO_COMMIT (2) the static GIT_BUILD_COMMIT, each only when cmake defined it (CPU always, COMMIT when `git rev-parse HEAD` succeeded at configure time); every other value, 0 included, returns NULL without setting an error. The returned strings are static, never freed. Rust: `BuildInfo` (#[repr(u32)], fallible from_raw) in core/common.rs.

types.name: git_checkout_options
types._comment_agent: Public options struct, caller-owned by value (stack or Rust storage); libgit2 never allocates or frees one it hands out. Init: git_checkout_options_init(opts, GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_VERSION) memcpys GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_INIT ({1}, rest zero) and fails (-1, GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'invalid version N on git_checkout_options') without touching *opts for version 0 or > 1; with version 1 it reaches no global, allocator or TLS. No destructor, disposer or cloner: every consumer takes `const git_checkout_options *` and copies by value (checkout_data_init memmoves it into data->opts, reset/worktree/merge/stash/cherrypick/revert copy and patch their local copy). Only internal copies own pointees: checkout_data owns `baseline` when it looked HEAD up itself (opts_free_baseline), and rebase_init_operation's rebase->options copy git_tree_dups `baseline` and git__strdups target_directory and the three labels, all released by git_rebase_free. C defects there (for the git_rebase batch): rebase memcpys `baseline_index` without a reference yet git_rebase_free calls git_index_free on it (drops the caller's reference); it keeps the caller's `paths` array, callbacks and payloads past the call; and its GIT_ERROR_CHECK_ALLOC tests the source label, not the copy. Wrapped in workdir/checkout.rs as the hand-written lifetime-carrying CheckoutOptions<'o> (+ Ref<'a,'o>/Mut<'a,'o>): strings, paths and baseline_index (as IndexRef<'o>) borrowed for 'o through safe setters; baseline and the callbacks+payloads as unsafe raw seams until git_tree and the checkout callbacks are wrapped.

ptr.note: Caller's label, borrowed and only read; NULL = "ancestor". Used in diff3/zdiff3 conflict markers. rebase's internal copy owns a git__strdup.

Caller's tree, borrowed for the checkout call and only read (git_iterator_for_tree); NULL (with baseline_index NULL) = HEAD's tree, which checkout looks up into its private copy and frees there (opts_free_baseline). rebase's internal copy owns a git_tree_dup reference released by git_rebase_free. The caller's struct never owns it.

Caller's index, borrowed for the checkout call; overrides baseline. Read through git_iterator_for_index(git_index_owner(idx), idx), which snapshots it (index readers count, entry sort under the index's own lock). Owned only by rebase's internal copy, wrongly: rebase memcpys the caller's pointer without git_index_owner/refcount increment and git_rebase_free git_index_frees it (C defect: drops a reference the rebase never took). Wrapped as a safe Option<IndexRef<'o>> setter/getter: libgit2's checkout counts a reference only for the call (git_index_snapshot_new/release), so an IndexBox stays sole once it returns.

Function pointer; NULL = no notifications (checkout_notify returns 0 when NULL or when `why & notify_flags` is 0). Called on the checkout thread, synchronously, during git_checkout_{head,index,tree} (and every API forwarding checkout options), with notify_payload; a non-zero return cancels the checkout and is returned (checkout_notify sets an error 'notify_cb' message when the callback set none).
Opaque user cookie, never dereferenced by libgit2; passed unchanged as notify_cb's last argument. Its type and mutability are the callback's.

Caller's label, borrowed and only read; NULL = "ours" (conflict markers and the ~ours side-file suffix). rebase's internal copy owns a git__strdup; stash and rebase fill their local copies with static labels.
Function pointer; NULL = no report. Called once at the end of a successful git_checkout_iterator with a pointer to checkout_data's perfdata (valid for the call only) and perfdata_payload.
Opaque user cookie for perfdata_cb, never dereferenced by libgit2.
Function pointer; NULL = no progress reports (report_progress checks it). Called synchronously from checkout with (path or NULL, completed, total, progress_payload).
Opaque user cookie for progress_cb, never dereferenced by libgit2.

Caller's path string, borrowed and only read during the call (data->opts copies the pointer; NULL = the repository workdir, and a bare repo is then refused). Created with mkdir when missing. rebase's internal copy owns a git__strdup released by git_rebase_free.
Caller's label, borrowed and only read; NULL = "theirs". rebase's internal copy owns a git__strdup.

types.name: git_commitarray
types._comment_agent: By-value C struct {commits, count}, never allocated by libgit2 itself (header: 'the library will never allocate that object directly'): callers own it inline. Producer: git_repository_commit_parents, which overwrites both fields (out->count = 0; out->commits = NULL) without releasing what they held, then git_vector_detach's a vector of git_commit_lookup references (exact size, git__reallocarray storage) on success; {NULL, 0} for an unborn HEAD and on every failure. Internal consumer create_from_tree (commit.c) passes parents.commits as const git_commit *[] and disposes. git_commitarray_dispose: NULL-tolerant, git_commit_free on each of the first count commits, git__free(commits), memset 0. All-zero is the empty array; dispose accepts it, but git__free(NULL) reads git__allocator unsynchronised against the first git_libgit2_init (see git_oidarray), so the Rust CommitArrayDispose skips C when commits is NULL (which also tolerates a NULL commits with count > 0, which C would dereference). Not address-sensitive. No refcount, no lock. Elements are git_commit references from the repository's object cache (git_object_free = git_cached_obj_decref); they outlive the repository (git_commit__free never touches repo). Wrapped (repository wave 0 batch 2) as CommitArray / CommitArrayVal = CVal<CommitArray, CommitArrayDispose> in object/commit.rs: new() (empty), unsafe from_raw(git_commitarray) adoption, into_raw, len/is_empty, commit_ptrs() -> CSlice<*mut git_commit> (raw seam until git_commit is wrapped), clear(). Not Send/Sync pending the git_commit run. C DEFECT (for the git_repository_commit_parents symbol run): on a failure after the first parent is collected (malformed MERGE_HEAD line, or a MERGE_HEAD id that is not a commit), the done: path frees the collected commits with git__free instead of git_commit_free while the repository's object cache still holds them: a later lookup of that commit (or the repository's cache teardown) is a heap-use-after-free (ASan-confirmed: git_repository_commit_parents repository.c:4135 frees, git_object_lookup_prefix -> cache_get reads).

ptr.note: Buffer of count git_commit pointers in libgit2's allocator (git_vector_detach of a git__reallocarray'd vector), owned by the struct and freed by git_commitarray_dispose with git__free after releasing each element. NULL with count 0 for an empty result (unborn HEAD, every failure). The pointer slots are never written after detach (git_commit *const *). Each element is one git_commit reference (git_commit_lookup / git_object_lookup), owned by the array and released by git_commitarray_dispose with git_commit_free (a cache decref); read-only through the array (create_from_tree passes them as const git_commit *[]).

types.name: git_config
types._comment_agent: Opaque (body in src/libgit2/config.h), heap-allocated, reference-counted: git_config_new git__calloc's it with readers/writers vectors and refcount 1; GIT_REFCOUNT_DEC in git_config_free frees it (config_free: down-refs each backend_instance, disposes vectors, git__free) only when the count reaches 0 AND rc.owner is NULL. No public up-ref. Producers of a sole reference: git_config_new, git_config_open_ondisk / open_default / open_level / open_global, git_config_snapshot, git_repository_config_snapshot. Shared reference: git_repository_config (GIT_REFCOUNT_INC on repo->_config, owner = repo; the repository writes through it, e.g. git_repository_set_workdir/set_bare via __weakptr). git_repository_set_config up-refs the caller's config and sets owner = repo, so a caller's sole reference stops being sole (its wrapper must take the shared owner). git_repository_free -> set_config(NULL) sets owner NULL before its down-ref, so the config outlives the repository. git_config_set_string reads GIT_REFCOUNT_OWNER(config) and clears the owner's configmap cache: a release of the owning repository on another thread races it (UAF), and nothing synchronises the backend vectors: neither Send nor Sync (docs/threading.md: only snapshots are shareable). git_config_lock's transaction and config iterators borrow the config (no ref). Wrapped (repository wave 0 batch 2) in config/config.rs as Config with ConfigFree (impl_cdrop git_config_free + CNew git_config_new, pinning the runtime first), ConfigBox = CBox (sole), ConfigArc = CArc (shared, no Clone), Config::new() -> Result<ConfigBox, ErrorBuf>.

types.name: git_error
types._comment_agent: Published only as `const git_error *` by git_error_last, which never returns NULL: a static error, or &error_threadstate.error of the calling thread, whose fields libgit2 overwrites on the next git_error_set*/git_error_clear on that thread, so a borrow is only valid until the next libgit2 call there and must not cross threads. klass is a git_error_t value stored as int. Its lifecycle routines (git_error_save = alloc constructor through out, git_error_free / git_error_restore = droppers, statics skipped by IS_STATIC_ERROR) are internal to libgit2.so (src/util/errors.h, hidden), so a wrapper copies a published error into Rust storage instead.

ptr.note: Runtime-conditional ownership. In every git_error libgit2 publishes (git_error_last) it is borrowed: for the per-thread error it aliases error_threadstate.message.ptr (a git_str the thread state owns; set_error_from_buffer), so it dangles once the next error on that thread grows the buffer (git_str_puts/vprintf realloc) and dies with the thread state (thread exit, git_libgit2_shutdown); for the four static errors (oom, uninitialized, tlsdata, no_error) it is a static string literal. Only in the private copies made by git_error_save is it owned: a git__strdup that git_error_free / git_error_restore release with git__free. Never NULL in a published error (the thread state's git_str is initialised to git_str__initstr and set_error_from_buffer is skipped on OOM); C callers (fetchhead_ref_parse, local_push, git_fs_path_direach) read it unchecked. Never written through: libgit2 writes the git_str and re-points the field.

types.name: git_error_code
types._comment_agent: Plain C enum (bindgen: c_int constants, values 0 and -1..-40 with gaps at -2 and -25..-29). No storage, no pointer, no lifecycle: libgit2 never names the type in a signature, every API returns or accepts these codes as plain int, and callbacks may return any int (positive values and unknown negatives are passed through, e.g. git_error_set_after_callback), so a raw int is not guaranteed to be a variant. GIT_EUSER is never produced by libgit2; GIT_RETRY is internal. Wrapped as a Rust enum whose discriminants are the bindgen constants, converted from int fallibly (from_raw -> Option) and never transmuted.

types.name: git_error_t
types._comment_agent: Plain C enum of error classes (bindgen: c_uint constants 0..=36, contiguous). No storage, no pointer, no lifecycle. Consumers carry it as int: git_error.klass (int, @type git_error_t) and git_error_set/git_error_set_str(int error_class, ...), which accept any int from user code, so git_error_last()->klass may hold a value outside the enum. Wrapped as a Rust enum with discriminants from the bindgen constants, converted from int fallibly (from_raw -> Option).

types.name: git_feature_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless bit-flag enum (1<<0 .. 1<<12), by value only; no pointer, no lifecycle (core wave 0 batch 1, 2026-10-09). Two consumers with different cardinality: git_libgit2_features (libgit2.c:83) returns an `int` OR-ing the compiled-in features (scalar set; HTTP_PARSER, REGEX, COMPRESSION, SHA1, SHA256 always), and git_libgit2_feature_backend (libgit2.c:118) takes ONE value and switches on it, returning a static backend string or NULL (unnamed values, combinations, HTTP always, and features compiled out). Its GIT_ASSERT_WITH_RETVAL branches (feature compiled in with an unknown backend) are unreachable in configured builds but would set an error (pre-init TLS hazard) or abort in Debug. Rust: `Feature` (#[repr(u32)] single value) and `Features` (c_int set, unnamed bits retained) in core/common.rs.

types.name: git_filemode_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum of octal UNIX modes (UNREADABLE 0, TREE 0040000, BLOB 0100644, BLOB_EXECUTABLE 0100755, LINK 0120000, COMMIT 0160000; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, pointers or lifecycle: passed and returned by value. Unnamed values flow through it: git_tree_entry_filemode_raw (tree.c:255) returns git_tree_entry.attr (uint16_t) as parsed by parse_mode (tree.c:371, any octal value 0..=0177777, larger -> git_tree_lookup -1 GIT_ERROR_TREE 'failed to parse tree: can't parse filemode'), e.g. old git's 0100664 or 0, which reads as UNREADABLE; git_tree_entry_filemode normalises (normalize_filemode, tree.c:35: type 04 -> TREE, any 0100 exec bit -> BLOB_EXECUTABLE before the 016/012 checks, so 0160755 -> BLOB_EXECUTABLE, else BLOB), always one of the five insertable values. git_treebuilder_insert (and git_tree_create_updated through it) accepts exactly TREE/BLOB/BLOB_EXECUTABLE/LINK/COMMIT (valid_filemode tree.c:26), refusing everything else, UNREADABLE included, with -1 GIT_ERROR_TREE 'failed to insert entry: invalid filemode for file - <name>' before touching the builder; with strict object creation on, TREE must name a tree and BLOB/EXEC/LINK a blob, COMMIT is unchecked. UNREADABLE marks an unreadable workdir file in iterator.c:1444. git_diff_file.mode (uint16_t) and git_index_entry.mode (uint32_t) carry these values untyped. Rust side (core/types.rs FileMode): never transmute; convert fallibly (FileMode::from_raw / TryFrom -> UnnamedFileMode); a tree-entry wrapper should return Result<FileMode, UnnamedFileMode> (or the raw u32) for filemode_raw and may expect a named value from filemode; a treebuilder insert wrapper taking FileMode must still expect UNREADABLE to be refused.

types.name: git_index
types._comment_agent: git_index is opaque in the public API (include/git2/types.h forward-declares it; only src/libgit2/index.h defines it), so a wrap publishes no field accessors. It is a refcounted heap object (rc, GIT_REFCOUNT_*): git_index_open / open_ext / new / new_ext calloc it and hand out the one reference (refcount 1, rc.owner NULL); merge/cherrypick/revert/apply results (git_merge_trees, git_merge_commits, git_cherrypick_commit, git_revert_commit, git_apply_to_tree) are such fresh indexes too. git_index_free is the down-ref: GIT_REFCOUNT_DEC frees through index_free once the count reaches 0 while rc.owner is NULL. Further references: git_repository_set_index retains one for the repository (and sets rc.owner = repo until the repository drops it), git_repository_index and git_rebase_inmemory_index hand out an extra counted reference to an index the repository/rebase keeps, and index iterators / indexwriters / git_checkout_index take temporary ones. There is no public up_ref, dup or readable count, so Rust holds a fresh index as CBox<Index, IndexFree> (sole reference: IndexMut available) and a counted reference to a shared index as CArc<Index, IndexFree> without Clone or get_mut (IndexRef only); a box converts into an arc before it is shared (set_index must take the arc, never IndexMut). git_index_owner lends rc.owner, a repository pointer that is NOT counted and is cleared when the repository releases the index. Not thread-safe: libgit2 serialises nothing but the refcount, so no Send/Sync. C notes: open_ext's failure path calls git_index_free on a refcount-0 index (dec to -1, freed: fine); index_free returns early, leaking, if readers > 0, unreachable through counted references since every reader holds one. Index-file reader defects reachable from git_index_open: read_entry leaks tmp_path (a version 4 entry's decompressed path) when the entry runs past the buffer (any truncated v4 file); an empty index_path is accepted and git_index_write on that index memcpys from a NULL path_original (git_filebuf_open_withsize, UBSan) - Index::open refuses ''. git_index_read's `(updated = git_futils_filestamp_check(..) < 0)` returns +1 when the file vanishes between exists and stat, so open then succeeds with an error set (race only).

ptr.note: git_vector_cmp function pointer: git__strcmp_cb or git__strcasecmp_cb (static functions), chosen by git_index_open_ext and git_index__set_ignore_case. Set before the index is handed out; never NULL on a live index. Not published.
git_vector_cmp function pointer: git_index_entry_srch / git_index_entry_isrch, chosen by open_ext and __set_ignore_case; never NULL on a live index. Not published.
git_vector_cmp function pointer: index_entry_srch_path / index_entry_isrch_path (static), chosen by open_ext and __set_ignore_case; never NULL on a live index. Not published.

The on-disk index path. git_index_open_ext git__strdup's the caller's index_path (never retained) and index_free releases it with git__free. NULL for an in-memory index (git_index_new / new_ext, and every merge/apply/cherrypick/revert result built on them), which git_index_read / write / git_indexwriter_init refuse ('the index is in-memory only'). Never reassigned after construction and never written through; git_index_path lends it (borrowed from the index) and read paths only pass it to the filesystem. Not published: the public header declares git_index opaque. An empty path is stored as given (Index::open refuses it: writing such an index is UB in git_filebuf_open_withsize).
git_vector_cmp function pointer: reuc_srch / reuc_isrch (static), chosen by open_ext and __set_ignore_case; never NULL on a live index. Not published.

The TREE extension's root git_tree_cache node. git_tree_cache_read / git_tree_cache_read_tree allocate the whole cache tree from index->tree_pool, so it is borrowed from that pool and never freed individually: every path that clears the pool (git_index_read, git_index_clear, git_index_read_tree, git_index_write_tree's read_tree path) first sets tree = NULL. NULL until a TREE extension is read or a tree is read in, and after any clear. Written through by git_tree_cache_invalidate_path (entry_count = -1 on every touched node) on add/remove/conflict paths. Not published.

types.name: git_libgit2_opt_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum of the keys git_libgit2_opts (settings.c:105) dispatches on, dense 0..=47 (GIT_OPT_GET_MWINDOW_SIZE .. GIT_OPT_SET_PACK_MAX_OBJECT_SIZE; bindgen types it c_uint, but git_libgit2_opts takes `int option, ...`). No storage or lifecycle. Every value without a constant (negative included) hits the default arm: -1, GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'invalid option key', and no va_arg is read, so calling with the bare key is sound. Each named key fixes the variadic argument list (documented per variant in core/common.rs LibraryOption). Hazards for the git_libgit2_opts wrapper: SET_SSL_CIPHERS strdups its argument with no NULL check (NULL = crash); SET_ALLOCATOR memcpys a git_allocator (NULL restores stdalloc) and swaps the global allocator under live allocations; GET/SET_WINDOWS_SHAREMODE are no-ops off Windows (the out pointer is left unwritten, rc 0); SET_SSL_CERT_LOCATIONS with OpenSSL fails GIT_ERROR_SSL when neither location loads; ADD_SSL_X509_CERT(NULL) adds nothing and returns 0; SET_SEARCH_PATH/GET_SEARCH_PATH take an int config level, only SYSTEM(2)/XDG(3)/GLOBAL(4) accepted (GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'invalid config path selector %d'); SET_SERVER_(CONNECT_)TIMEOUT refuse negatives (GIT_ERROR_INVALID); SET_OWNER_VALIDATION stores !=0; GET_EXTENSIONS hands out a git_strarray to dispose; GET_* buf options fill a git_buf. Settings are unsynchronised globals (git_sysdir_set etc.). Rust side: LibraryOption::from_raw/from_key/TryFrom -> UnnamedLibraryOption; key() gives the int.

types.name: git_object_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_OBJECT_ANY = -2, GIT_OBJECT_INVALID = -1, COMMIT 1, TREE 2, BLOB 3, TAG 4; bindgen types it c_int). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle: passed and returned by value, and through out-params (git_odb_read_header, git_odb_read_prefix-style backend callbacks in sys/odb_backend.h, git_odb_expand_id.type in/out). Only 1..=4 name an object's type: git_object_type_is_valid (object.c:344) accepts exactly those (git_objects_table size > 0); type2string gives '' for any other value; string2type returns INVALID for unknown, NULL or empty names (it prefix-matches, so 'commitx' -> COMMIT). GIT_OBJECT_ANY is a lookup/peel filter only (object_lookup*, git_object_peel, git_reference_peel, tree_entry_to_object, odb expand_ids), never an object's type; INVALID is an error/unset answer (git_object_type(NULL), git_tag_target_type(NULL), git_tree_entry_type(NULL), string2type misses, parse placeholders). The pack-entry types 6/7 are the GIT_PACKFILE_OFS_DELTA/REF_DELTA macros (pack.h:37), packfile-only, never a public out-param; cache.c's per-type limit table still reserves slots 0 and 5..7, so GIT_OPT_SET_CACHE_OBJECT_LIMIT accepts any of 0..=7 and rejects others 'type out of range' (cache.c:36). git_odb_expand_ids reads 0 as ANY and writes 0 back on a miss. HAZARD (probed, plain build): git_odb_write(..., type 0) succeeds - normalize_options (object.c:630) reads object_type 0 as BLOB for the id, but the loose backend formats its header from type2string(0) = '', so it stores an object under a blob id that git_odb_read_header then fails on ('failed to read loose object header'), and a later real write of the same blob is skipped by git_odb__freshen. Every other unnamed value (<0, >=5) is rejected 'invalid object type'. Rust side (core/types.rs): ObjectType {Commit, Tree, Blob, Tag}, #[repr(i32)], non_exhaustive; never transmute: from_raw/TryFrom<git_object_t> -> NotAnObjectType for every other value; filters spell ANY as None through ObjectType::raw_or_any(Option<ObjectType>), so a typed write/hash wrapper cannot pass 0.

types.name: git_odb
types._comment_agent: git_odb is opaque in the public API (typedef in git2/types.h, body in src/libgit2/odb.h) and reference counted: rc.refcount is an atomic count, rc.owner an atomically swapped back-pointer to the git_repository that installed it (GIT_REFCOUNT_OWN). Constructors git_odb_new / git_odb_new_ext (git__calloc, count 1, no backends) and git_odb_open / git_odb_open_ext (new + loose and pack backends for objects_dir, its commit-graph and info/alternates, recursively up to depth 5; a missing objects_dir fails GIT_ERROR_ODB "failed to load object database in '<dir>'", *out NULL; missing alternates are skipped). Dropper git_odb_free = GIT_REFCOUNT_DEC: atomic decrement, and odb_free (every backend's own free, cgraph, vector, own_cache, mutex, then git__free) only once the count reaches 0 AND no repository owns it. libgit2 exports no up_ref: references are multiplied only by git_repository_odb (+1 to the repo's odb, lazily created by git_repository_odb__weakptr), git_repository_set_odb / git_repository_wrap_odb (repo takes +1 and becomes owner). So a Rust owner is a CArc without Clone (OdbArc = CArc<Odb, OdbFree>), never a CBox: a repository may share it at any time. Thread safety (docs/threading.md: 'git_odb uses locking internally'): backends and cgraph are only touched under db->lock (a non-recursive pthread mutex); own_cache is a git_cache under its own rwlock; options are written only by git_odb_new_ext before publication; do_fsync only by git_odb__set_caps on a repository-private odb before the CAS publishes it; refcount and owner are atomics. Every public routine takes the lock itself, so all of them go on the shared handle (OdbRef); nothing hands out OdbMut. Hazards for the symbol batches: odb_cache() loads rc.owner and then uses &owner->objects without holding a reference to the owner, so freeing the owning repository on another thread while this odb (held through its own reference) is read races a use-after-free of the repo's object cache; git_repository_odb__weakptr leaks the new odb (owner already set, so the free does not release it) and odb_path when git_odb__set_caps or add_default_backends fails, and leaks odb_path when repository_odb_alternates fails; git_odb__add_default_backends leaks the loose (resp. pack) backend when add_backend_internal fails (OOM only); git_repository_wrap_odb GIT_ASSERTs a valid options.oid_type; git_odb_new_ext stores an unnamed non-zero opts->oid_type unvalidated. Wave 0 type review (2026-10-10): the owner-cache race above is reachable through the wrapper types alone (OdbRef is Send since Odb is Sync; Repository being !Send does not order the free after a reader on another thread), confirmed by ASan (heap-use-after-free in cache_get from git_odb_exists_ext, crustify/reviews/.../repository/wave-0/batch-0/unsafe/odb-sync-proof-omits-owner-repository-cache). Representation: Odb<'r> / OdbRef<'a,'r> / OdbMut<'a,'r> / OdbArc<'r> borrow the OWNING repository (hand-written CCell like Refdb<'r>); constructors give OdbArc<'static> (no owner). Contract for the symbol batches: git_repository_odb returns OdbArc<'r>; git_repository_set_odb / git_repository_wrap_odb consume an OdbArc<'static> (the only proof no repository owns the odb; a second owner would leave the first reading a cache it does not hold) and may hand it back as OdbArc<'r>.

ptr.note: The odb's commit-graph, NULL until git_odb__add_default_backends lazily opens one for the first on-disk objects dir (git_commit_graph_new) or git_odb_set_commit_graph installs a caller's (ownership transferred, previous one freed with git_commit_graph_free). Released by odb_free. Read and replaced only under db->lock (git_odb__get_commit_graph_file, set_commit_graph, add_default_backends).

types.name: git_oid
types._comment_agent: Plain value type with no pointer fields: `type` (unsigned char holding a git_oid_t value, 0 = GIT_OID_NONE/unset) and `id` (32-byte inline array, GIT_OID_MAX_SIZE). Never heap-allocated by libgit2's public API on its own; callers hold it by value or receive `const git_oid *` into a parent object. Nothing to release. Every bit pattern is accepted by oid.c: an unknown `type` makes git_oid_size/hexsize return 0 and the formatters report 'unknown type' (git_oid_nfmt/pathfmt) - BUT git_oid_tostr_s then returns its per-thread buffer without writing it (uninitialised on the thread's first call, no NUL: ASan heap-buffer-overflow in strlen confirmed with a zeroed oid), so its wrapper must reject unknown types. All-zero is libgit2's own GIT_OID_NONE. Constructors (init into caller storage): git_oid_from_string, git_oid_from_prefix, git_oid_from_raw; cloner: git_oid_cpy (memcpy of the whole struct; overlapping out/src would be UB).

types.name: git_oid_shorten
types._comment_agent: Opaque in the public API (forward-declared in git2/oid.h, defined in oid.c); only oid.c touches its fields. Constructor git_oid_shorten_new (git__calloc + 16-node trie; NULL on OOM or when min_length does not fit an int - a hard assert(3) in _DEBUG builds), dropper git_oid_shorten_free (NULL-safe). No cloner. git_oid_shorten_add keeps borrowed pointers into its text_oid argument and validates only the characters it walks, so a short or non-hex id stored as a tail later yields git__fromhex == -1 and push_leaf writes children[-1], silently corrupting the preceding trie node (in bounds of the buffer, so ASan does not flag it; probe: add("azzz") then add("ab0...0") both succeed): its wrapper must accept only full 40-char hex ids, borrowed for the shortener's lifetime.

ptr.note: Trie buffer of `size` trie_node unions, allocated by resize_trie through git__reallocarray and released by git_oid_shorten_free (git__free). Each node is either 16 child indices or a leaf whose `tail` is a BORROWED `const char *` into a text id the caller passed to git_oid_shorten_add (retained after the call: the shortener reads the tail again when a later id shares the prefix), so the shortener must not outlive any string added to it. NULL after a failed resize inside git_oid_shorten_add: resize_trie assigns the realloc result before checking it, leaking the old buffer and leaving nodes == NULL with size unchanged, so the next add dereferences NULL; only git_oid_shorten_free remains safe on such an object.

types.name: git_oid_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_OID_SHA1 = 1, GIT_OID_SHA256 = 2, both unconditional in include/git2/oid.h; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle: passed and returned by value. Unnamed values flow through it: 0 means 'unset' in every *_options.oid_type - read as GIT_OID_DEFAULT (SHA1) by repository.c:356/364 (git_repository_new, which GIT_ASSERT_ARGs validity of a non-zero value), odb.c:307, index.c:447, commit_graph.c:431 and midx.c:537 (both assert validity after defaulting), indexer.c:178, object.c:633, diff_parse.c:91, but as the repository's own type by git_diff_options (diff_generate.c:502: 0 -> repo->oid_type, a non-zero mismatch is GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'specified object ID type does not match repository object ID type'). Public routines also hand 0 out: git_repository_oid_type(NULL) returns 0 (repository.c:4076) and git_remote_oid_type writes *out = 0 before failing (remote.c:1040); git_oid_type_fromstr/fromstrn return 0 for an unknown name (load_objectformat -> GIT_EINVALID 'unknown object format'). git_repository_init_ext validates opts->oid_type not at all (repository.c:2936): an unnamed value is written to extensions.objectformat as git_oid_type_name's 'unknown' and the just-created repository fails to open (GIT_EINVALID, directory left behind). git_oid_size/hexsize/type_is_valid reject anything but 1 and 2 (src/libgit2/oid.h:27-54), so git_oid_from_* return -1 'unknown type'. git_oid.type stores it narrowed to unsigned char. Rust side: never transmute; convert fallibly (OidType::from_raw / TryFrom<git_oid_t>); option-field accessors should map 0 to None and typed setters make the init_ext quirk unreachable; returned values go through from_raw too.

types.name: git_oidarray
types._comment_agent: By-value C struct {ids, count}, never allocated by libgit2 itself (header: 'the library will never allocate that object directly'): callers own it inline and dispose its ids with git_oidarray_dispose. All-zero is the empty array and dispose accepts it (git__free(NULL)); before git_libgit2_init git__free is failalloc's no-op, but git__free reads git__allocator.gfree unsynchronised, and the first git_libgit2_init (git_allocator_global_init -> git_stdalloc_init_allocator) or GIT_OPT_SET_ALLOCATOR writes it: disposing an empty array on one thread while another thread initialises the library is a data race (TSan, oid review wave 1 batch 0). Only the empty array can reach that, since nothing allocated for it; the Rust OidArrayDispose therefore skips the C call when ids is NULL. count must not exceed the buffer's length; ids must be non-NULL when count > 0 (git_repository__shallow_roots_write indexes it unconditionally). Not address-sensitive. No refcount, no lock. Deprecated alias git_oidarray_free is compiled hidden under DEPRECATE_HARD. Wrapped as OidArray / OidArrayVal = CVal<OidArray, OidArrayDispose> with ids moved in/out as OdbDataVec<Oid> (git_odb_backend_data_alloc/free = git__malloc/git__free).

ptr.note: A buffer of `count` git_oid values in libgit2's allocator (git__allocator), owned by the struct and released by git_oidarray_dispose -> git__free (which does not reset the fields). Producers: git_merge_bases / git_merge_bases_many hand over a git_array_oid_t's ptr (git_oidarray__from_array; grown by git__reallocarray, so asize may exceed count), git_smart__shallow_roots git__malloc's a copy (NULL for 0). NULL whenever count == 0 on every libgit2 path (git_array_init leaves ptr NULL until the first alloc; smart sets NULL); fetch.c/compute_base start from {0}. Elements are written in place (git_oidarray__reverse), read by index (git_repository__shallow_roots_write, oidarray_contains, compute_base). A transport's shallow_roots callback (git2/sys/transport.h) fills `out` with an allocation libgit2 later frees with git_oidarray_dispose, so a user-filled array must be git__malloc storage (git_odb_backend_data_alloc is the exported route). git_oidarray__to_array lends the buffer to a git_array without transferring ownership.

types.name: git_path_fs
types._comment_agent: Plain C enum (GENERIC=0, NTFS=1, HFS=2), passed by value; no lifecycle. Its only reader is git_path_is_gitfile (path.c), which switches on it: GENERIC = the NTFS check || the HFS check, NTFS = validate_dotgit_ntfs_generic only, HFS = validate_dotgit_hfs_generic only; any other value fails -1 with GIT_ERROR_OS 'invalid filesystem for path validation' (after the gitfile range check, which fails first with 'invalid gitfile for path validation'). libgit2 itself calls it with HFS and NTFS for .gitmodules (path.c validate_repo_component). Rust: Filesystem enum with from_raw/raw/TryFrom (UnnamedFilesystem). Hazard for the git_path_is_gitfile symbol batch: the NTFS branch ignores pathlen - it reads name[6], name[7], up to name[8] and ntfs_end_of_filename scans to NUL or ':' - so a path slice that is not NUL-terminated within reach is read out of bounds; the HFS branch honours pathlen. A safe wrapper must pass a NUL-terminated copy (&CStr) and its length.

types.name: git_path_gitfile
types._comment_agent: Fieldless enum; git_path_is_gitfile indexes path.c's gitfiles[] table (gitignore, gitmodules, gitattributes) with the raw value and refuses anything outside 0..=2 with GIT_ERROR_OS "invalid gitfile for path validation" (plus errno text), returning -1. Rust: GitFile with fallible from_raw. Note for git_path_is_gitfile's wrapper: its NTFS checks (validate_dotgit_ntfs_generic) read name[6], name[7] and up to a NUL regardless of pathlen, so the path must be NUL-terminated.

types.name: git_refdb
types._comment_agent: Opaque in the public API (forward-declared in git2/types.h, defined in src/libgit2/refdb.h). Refcounted (rc) with an owner slot: GIT_REFCOUNT_DEC frees only when the count reaches 0 and rc.owner is NULL; a repository's own refdb is owned (GIT_REFCOUNT_OWN in set_refdb / git_repository_refdb__weakptr) and freed when the repository clears ownership and drops its reference. Public lifecycle: constructors git_refdb_open (with the backend the repo's refdb_type names) and git_refdb_new (no backend; usable only after git_refdb_set_backend), down-ref git_refdb_free (NULL-safe). No public up_ref: git_repository_refdb hands out a new reference (GIT_REFCOUNT_INC) and git_repository_set_refdb takes one. Rust: Refdb<'r> borrowing the repository for 'r, RefdbBox (sole: new/open) and RefdbArc (shared, no Clone) under RefdbFree = git_refdb_free; Refdb::new = git_refdb_new + git_refdb_set_backend so no handle designates a backendless refdb.

ptr.note: Owned vtable-headed backend, released through its own `free` member by refdb_free_backend (git_refdb__free, and git_refdb_set_backend before replacing it). NULL after git_refdb_new until git_refdb_set_backend: every routine reaching the backend (git_refdb_compress, lookup, write, init...) dereferences it unchecked, so a backendless refdb segfaults on git_refdb_compress (probed). git_refdb_set_backend takes ownership only on success (version check, required members, lock without unlock refused with GIT_EINVALID leave it to the caller); setting the same backend again frees it and keeps the dangling pointer.

Back pointer to the repository the refdb was built for (git_refdb_new/git_refdb_open store their repo argument; git_repository_set_refdb does not update it). Not refcounted: the refdb borrows the repository, whose config cache, paths and odb its backends (which keep the same pointer) read and update on every reference operation, so a refdb must not be used after its repository is freed. Never NULL (GIT_ASSERT_ARG on construction). Freeing a refdb does not touch it with the files or reftable backend.

types.name: git_refdb_t
types._comment_agent: C enum passed by value (git_repository_init_options.refdb_type, git_repository.refdb_type). 0 in init options means the default (files); git_refdb_type_fromstr returns 0 for an unknown extensions.refstorage value, which git_repository_open then rejects. No pointer fields, no lifecycle. Wrapped as RefdbType in refs/refdb.rs (fallible from_raw / TryFrom).

types.name: git_reference
types._comment_agent: Opaque in the public API (forward-declared in git2/types.h; body in src/libgit2/refs.h), so no field is published and the wrapper exposes none. Sole-owner heap object: git__calloc'd with the name as a flexible array (alloc_ref), released by git_reference_free (frees target.symbolic for a symbolic ref, down-refs db, frees the struct; NULL is a no-op); deep-copied by git_reference_dup (re-allocates through git_reference__alloc(_symbolic) and up-refs the SAME db; *dest NULL and -1 on OOM). Not refcounted itself. Two statically distinct kinds: ATTACHED references (every reference the non-sys public API hands out: lookup, create, dwim, resolve, rename, set_target, iterators, foreach, git_repository_head, dup) carry a counted db; DETACHED references (git_reference__alloc / git_reference__alloc_symbolic from git2/sys/refs.h, for refdb backends) have db NULL until git_refdb lookup/iterator/write attaches them, and git_reference_dup (GIT_REFCOUNT_INC(NULL)) and git_reference_owner (db->repo) crash on them. A reference keeps its refdb alive past the repository (set_refdb OWN(NULL)+DEC on repo free), but db->repo and the fs backend's repo then dangle, so owner/resolve/rename/delete/set_target/peel are use-after-free once the repository is freed: the Rust wrapper is Reference<'r>, tied to the repository borrow, and DetachedReference for the sys allocators. Wrapped in refs/refs.rs (repository wave 0 batch 6).

ptr.note: A counted reference on the refdb: git_refdb_lookup / resolve / iterator_next / write / rename, git_reference_lookup_resolved (pseudorefs) and git_reference_dup GIT_REFCOUNT_INC it when storing; git_reference_free GIT_REFCOUNT_DECs it (freeing the refdb once the count drops and the repository no longer owns it). NULL for a reference fresh from git_reference__alloc(_symbolic) (sys/refs.h) until a refdb attaches it; git_reference_free accepts NULL, git_reference_dup and every db->repo reader (owner, delete, rename, set_target, symbolic_set_target, resolve, peel) do not. Written through only by the refcount operations. The refdb's `repo` back-pointer is not counted, so it dangles once the repository is freed while the reference lives.

Union member, live only while type == GIT_REFERENCE_SYMBOLIC (otherwise the union holds target.oid). git__strdup'd by git_reference__alloc_symbolic (which fails and frees the struct when the copy fails, so a symbolic ref never holds NULL); freed by git_reference_free only for symbolic refs. Read-only after construction (git_reference_symbolic_target, dup, resolve).

types.name: git_reference_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_REFERENCE_INVALID = 0, DIRECT = 1, SYMBOLIC = 2, ALL = DIRECT|SYMBOLIC = 3; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle. Its only public flow is the return of git_reference_type (refs.c:339), which answers ref->type: DIRECT or SYMBOLIC for every git_reference libgit2 builds (git_reference__alloc / __alloc_symbolic, refs.c:60/85); with NULL it GIT_ASSERT_ARGs, returning -1 (u32::MAX through the unsigned enum) in a release build and aborting in the Debug/coverage build. INVALID is internal only (transaction.c node with no target set); ALL is a list-filter mask that no non-deprecated API takes (only deprecated GIT_REF_LISTALL). No public routine takes a git_reference_t argument. Rust side (core/types.rs): ReferenceType {Direct, Symbolic}, #[repr(u32)], non_exhaustive; from_raw/TryFrom<git_reference_t> -> NotAReferenceType for INVALID, ALL and every unnamed value; never transmute.

types.name: git_repository
types._comment_agent: git_repository is opaque to the public API (forward-declared in git2/types.h): no field is published, so the Rust wrapper (repository/repository.rs, Repository/RepositoryRef/RepositoryMut + RepositoryBox = CBox<Repository, RepositoryFree>) exposes no field accessor. No refcount: git_repository_free is the only release (sole owner), and nothing copies a repository. Constructors: git_repository_new/new_ext (allocation only, bare, no paths), open/open_ext/open_bare, init/init_ext, wrap_odb, open_from_worktree, plus git_clone/git_submodule_open elsewhere. C defects found: git_repository_open_bare leaks the half-built repository (and its path strings) when read_repository_format fails (e.g. unsupported core.repositoryformatversion or unknown extension), and when git_str_detach fails; init_ext can fail after git_repository_open succeeded, leaving a live repository in *out that the caller must free. Objects spawned from a repository (git_object, git_reference...) keep a raw repo pointer without a count: freeing the repository first makes their repo-dependent accessors UB, so their wrappers must borrow the repository.

ptr.note: The repository holds ONE counted reference: set_config does GIT_REFCOUNT_OWN(x, repo) + GIT_REFCOUNT_INC on the new value and atomically swaps it in, then GIT_REFCOUNT_OWN(old, NULL) + git_config_free (a down-ref) on the old one. Lazily loaded on first use (git_repository_config__weakptr, CAS from NULL; the loser frees its own). Public getters (git_repository_config) hand the caller a further counted reference; __weakptr callers borrow without one. git_repository__cleanup / git_repository_free drop the repository's reference and null the object's owner back-pointer, so a caller's reference outlives the repository safely.

The repository holds ONE counted reference: set_index does GIT_REFCOUNT_OWN(x, repo) + GIT_REFCOUNT_INC on the new value and atomically swaps it in, then GIT_REFCOUNT_OWN(old, NULL) + git_index_free (a down-ref) on the old one. Lazily loaded on first use (git_repository_index__weakptr, CAS from NULL; the loser frees its own). Public getters (git_repository_index) hand the caller a further counted reference; __weakptr callers borrow without one. git_repository__cleanup / git_repository_free drop the repository's reference and null the object's owner back-pointer, so a caller's reference outlives the repository safely.

The repository holds ONE counted reference: set_odb does GIT_REFCOUNT_OWN(x, repo) + GIT_REFCOUNT_INC on the new value and atomically swaps it in, then GIT_REFCOUNT_OWN(old, NULL) + git_odb_free (a down-ref) on the old one. Lazily loaded on first use (git_repository_odb__weakptr, CAS from NULL; the loser frees its own). Public getters (git_repository_odb) hand the caller a further counted reference; __weakptr callers borrow without one. git_repository__cleanup / git_repository_free drop the repository's reference and null the object's owner back-pointer, so a caller's reference outlives the repository safely.

The repository holds ONE counted reference: set_refdb does GIT_REFCOUNT_OWN(x, repo) + GIT_REFCOUNT_INC on the new value and atomically swaps it in, then GIT_REFCOUNT_OWN(old, NULL) + git_refdb_free (a down-ref) on the old one. Lazily loaded on first use (git_repository_refdb__weakptr, CAS from NULL; the loser frees its own). Public getters (git_repository_refdb) hand the caller a further counted reference; __weakptr callers borrow without one. git_repository__cleanup / git_repository_free drop the repository's reference and null the object's owner back-pointer, so a caller's reference outlives the repository safely.

Lazily created by git_attr_cache__init with an atomic compare-and-swap from NULL; git_attr_cache_flush (from git_repository__cleanup) atomically swaps it out and frees it. Owned, never shared out of the repository.
Common dir (differs from gitdir for worktrees); set at open, NULL for new/wrap_odb repos and when find_repo produced none. Freed by git_repository_free.
Lazily created by git_repository_driver_registry with an atomic CAS from NULL (loser frees its copy); freed by git_repository_free (git_diff_driver_registry_free).
Repository directory with trailing slash; set by open_ext/open_bare (git_str_detach), NULL for git_repository_new/new_ext/wrap_odb repos. Freed by git_repository_free.

Path of the .git file a worktree/submodule gitlink pointed through; git_str_detach'd by open_ext only when find_repo found a gitlink, else NULL. Freed by git_repository_free (git__free). Never replaced after open.
Loaded by load_grafts at open (info/grafts), freed and NULLed by git_repository__cleanup (git_grafts_free). Handed out only as a weak pointer (git_repository_grafts__weakptr).
Identity email override from git_repository_set_ident (as ident_name). Freed by git_repository_free.
Identity name override from git_repository_set_ident (git__free old, git__strdup new, NULL clears). Freed by git_repository_free.
Reference namespace; NULL unless git_repository_set_namespace (git__free old + git__strdup new, NULL clears) or GIT_NAMESPACE under OPEN_FROM_ENV. Freed by git_repository_free.

git_array_t(git_str) buffer: repository_alloc sizes it to 4 (alloc failure fails the constructor, so non-NULL on every live repository); git_repository__reserved_names appends git_str values it owns. git_repository_free disposes each element (git_str_dispose) then git_array_clear frees the buffer.
Loaded by load_grafts at open (shallow file), freed and NULLed by git_repository__cleanup (git_grafts_free). Weak pointers only (git_repository_shallow_grafts__weakptr).
Set by git_repository_submodule_cache_all (git_submodule_cache_init), freed and NULLed by git_repository_submodule_cache_clear, which git_repository__cleanup calls. Not synchronised.

Working directory with trailing slash; NULL for bare repos. load_workdir/git_repository_set_workdir replace it, git__free'ing the old string (set_workdir), git_repository_set_bare frees and NULLs it. Freed by git_repository_free.

types.name: git_repository_init_flag_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless bit-flag enum (BARE 1<<0, NO_REINIT 1<<1, MKDIR 1<<3, MKPATH 1<<4, EXTERNAL_TEMPLATE 1<<5, RELATIVE_GITLINK 1<<6; bindgen c_uint), by value only; no pointer, no lifecycle (repository wave 0 batch 8, 2026-10-10). Consumer: the uint32_t git_repository_init_options.flags, read by git_repository_init_ext (repository.c:2923) and its helpers; git_repository_init sets MKPATH(|BARE). Probed: init_ext ORs repository.h's internal bits into the CALLER's options (1<<16 HAS_DOTGIT, 1<<17 NATURAL_WD in repo_init_directories, 1<<18 IS_REINIT on reinit) and honours them on the next call with those options (a caller-set 1<<17 skips the gitlink/core.worktree); a reused options struct therefore carries IS_REINIT. MKPATH's bit equals GIT_REPOSITORY_OPEN_FROM_ENV, which init_ext also tests on the same flags: lookup_commondir reads $GIT_COMMON_DIR (with it naming a repo, a HEAD-only dir reads as a repository under MKPATH (NO_REINIT -> GIT_EEXISTS) but is initialised under MKDIR), and repo_init_config passes use_env only to repo_init_fs_configs -> are_symlinks_supported (repository.c:2236), whose global/system config load of core.symlinks is inside #ifdef GIT_WIN32; elsewhere the parameter is GIT_UNUSED, so on this platform MKPATH makes init read NO configuration from the environment (corrected by the wave 0 type review, 2026-10-10; batch 8 said it loads global/system config from the environment). Unnamed bits are never rejected. Rust: InitFlag (#[repr(u32)] single flag, fallible from_raw -> UnnamedInitFlag) and InitFlags (u32 set, from_bits_retain keeps unnamed bits, from_bits_truncate drops them) in repository/repository.rs; the options wrapper should read flags back with from_bits_retain and may want to strip internal bits on set.

types.name: git_repository_init_mode_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless enum of named modes (SHARED_UMASK 0, SHARED_GROUP 02775, SHARED_ALL 02777; bindgen c_uint) for the uint32_t git_repository_init_options.mode, which takes ANY value as a custom permission mode; no pointer, no lifecycle (repository wave 0 batch 8, 2026-10-10). Consumers: pick_dir_mode (repository.c:2579: UMASK->0777, GROUP->02775, ALL->02777, else the value), repo_init_config (GROUP writes core.sharedrepository=1 + receive.denyNonFastforwards, ALL =2 + the same; custom writes nothing), repo_init_structure (any non-UMASK mode chmods the built-in template's leaf dirs and an external template's dirs to the mode exactly), repo_init_directories (repo dir chmod'ed only when the mode has S_ISGID; MKDIR/MKPATH parents get mode & ~S_ISGID, MKPATH ancestors also & ~0002, all trimmed by umask), refdb_fs/refdb_reftable init (same mapping; refs dirs created umask-trimmed). A custom value equal to a named constant is that constant. Rust: InitMode enum {SharedUmask (default), SharedGroup, SharedAll, Custom(CustomMode)} in repository/repository.rs; from_raw is total and canonical (CustomMode never holds a named value, private field), raw() round-trips every u32.

types.name: git_repository_init_options
types._comment_agent: Plain options value, never allocated or freed by libgit2: callers build it on the stack with git_repository_init_options_init (GIT_REPOSITORY_INIT_OPTIONS_INIT) and pass it by non-const pointer. git_repository_init_ext WRITES opts->flags (ORs internal bits 1<<16 HAS_DOTGIT, 1<<17 NATURAL_WD, 1<<18 IS_REINIT), so the call needs exclusive access; reused options carry those bits into the next call (behavioural, no UB). oid_type/refdb_type 0 = default; unnamed values are not validated by init_ext (written as 'unknown', then the open of the result fails). git_repository_init_options_init has no NULL check (memcpy to NULL). Wrapped as InitOptions<'o> (repository/repository.rs): strings borrowed for 'o as &'o CStr, typed OidType/RefdbType/InitFlags/InitMode setters. Reinitialising with origin_url set fails GIT_EEXISTS ('remote 'origin' already exists') AFTER the inner open, leaving the live repository in *out (caller must free); description is only written from the built-in template on a fresh init (external template / reinit ignore it); template_path "" copies nothing and a missing explicit template dir falls back to the built-in one. Review (wave 1 type review): a template_path that lstat refuses as invalid (ENAMETOOLONG: a component over NAME_MAX) fails the init with GIT_EINVALIDSPEC (-12, GIT_ERROR_OS 'invalid path for filesystem ...') after repo_init_directories created the repository directory and before anything is written into it; only ENOENT/ENOTDIR (a missing dir, or a regular file) is the silent built-in fallback. NULL initial_head reads init.defaultbranch and NULL template_path (with EXTERNAL_TEMPLATE) reads init.templatedir from the global config, whose location sysdir caches from $HOME/$XDG_CONFIG_HOME at git_libgit2_init (tests/equiv/repository.rs init_options::defaults_read_the_global_configuration_as_c).

ptr.note: Read by repo_init_structure: replaces the template's description file content (strcmp against tpl path). Caller-owned NUL-terminated string, only read during the git_repository_init_ext call the options are passed to (also the internal submodule_repo_init/create, which point it at stack/borrowed strings); libgit2 never stores, frees or writes through it. NULL selects the default.

Read by get_initial_head, prefixed with refs/heads/ unless it starts with refs/, and git__strdup'ed before use; on reinit only a non-NULL value resets HEAD. Caller-owned NUL-terminated string, only read during the git_repository_init_ext call the options are passed to (also the internal submodule_repo_init/create, which point it at stack/borrowed strings); libgit2 never stores, frees or writes through it. NULL selects the default.

Passed to git_remote_create (which copies it) after init succeeds. Caller-owned NUL-terminated string, only read during the git_repository_init_ext call the options are passed to (also the internal submodule_repo_init/create, which point it at stack/borrowed strings); libgit2 never stores, frees or writes through it. NULL selects the default.

Read by repo_init_structure as the external template dir; non-NULL also forces external template use like GIT_REPOSITORY_INIT_EXTERNAL_TEMPLATE. Caller-owned NUL-terminated string, only read during the git_repository_init_ext call the options are passed to (also the internal submodule_repo_init/create, which point it at stack/borrowed strings); libgit2 never stores, frees or writes through it. NULL selects the default.

Read by repo_init_directories (git_fs_path_join_unrooted, relative to the repo path) and to decide whether to add .git. Caller-owned NUL-terminated string, only read during the git_repository_init_ext call the options are passed to (also the internal submodule_repo_init/create, which point it at stack/borrowed strings); libgit2 never stores, frees or writes through it. NULL selects the default.

types.name: git_repository_item_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum GITDIR 0 .. WORKTREE_CONFIG 14 plus the sentinel GIT_REPOSITORY_ITEM__LAST 15 (bindgen: c_uint). No storage, pointers or lifecycle: passed by value only. Sole public consumer git_repository_item_path (repository.c:3311 -> git_repository__item_path, :3319) indexes the static items[15] table (repository.c:46, {parent, fallback, name, directory}) with the value UNCHECKED: __LAST and every larger value read out of bounds (UBSan 'index 15 out of bounds for type ...[15]' at repository.c:3323, confirmed with the asan-ubsan build, batch 9 of libgit2/repository wave 0, 2026-10-10). Within bounds, resolved_parent_path maps the parent GITDIR/WORKDIR/COMMONDIR to git_repository_path/workdir/commondir (any other parent value: GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'invalid item directory', unreachable from the table); a NULL parent falls back to the entry's fallback (GITDIR for the commondir-rooted items and WORKTREE_CONFIG), else GIT_ENOTFOUND + GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'path cannot exist in repository' (WORKDIR of a bare repo). Directories get a trailing '/'; the commondir link is resolved (worktree COMMONDIR = main/.git/). Internal callers pass named constants only. Rust: `Item` (#[repr(u32)], #[non_exhaustive], 15 variants, no sentinel) with `ALL` indexed by value, fallible `from_raw`/TryFrom (UnnamedItem) refusing >= __LAST, in repository/repository.rs.

types.name: git_repository_new_options
types._comment_agent: Pointer-free 8-byte options value (version + git_oid_t), never allocated or freed by libgit2; read-only by git_repository_new_ext (version check, then GIT_ASSERT_ARG(git_oid_type_is_valid) for a non-zero oid_type: an unnamed value aborts the Debug/coverage build and fails -1 otherwise). 0 = GIT_OID_DEFAULT. Wrapped as NewOptions (repository/sys/repository.rs) with an Option<OidType> setter so only 0 or a named type is stored.

types.name: git_repository_open_flag_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless bit-flag enum NO_SEARCH 1, CROSS_FS 2, BARE 4, NO_DOTGIT 8, FROM_ENV 16 (bindgen: c_uint). No storage, pointers or lifecycle. Consumed as the `unsigned int flags` of git_repository_open_ext (repository.c:1157; find_repo/find_repo_traverse/lookup_commondir/is_valid_repository_path take it as uint32_t) and internally by git_repository_open (NO_SEARCH), git_repository_discover (CROSS_FS when across_fs), submodule.c:1635 (NO_SEARCH|BARE) and the CLI (FROM_ENV). Only the five named bits are tested; any other bit is ignored (equivalence-tested with 1<<5|1<<31). Observed semantics that differ from the header: FROM_ENV does NOT ignore the other flags (NO_SEARCH/BARE still apply) and replaces ceiling_dirs only when it is NULL; BARE (like NO_DOTGIT) makes the first iteration try start_path itself without appending .git (so a working dir with BARE|NO_SEARCH is ENOTFOUND), parents still get .git first; BARE also leaves no workdir. Cross-enum quirk: repo_init_config (repository.c:2377) tests GIT_REPOSITORY_OPEN_FROM_ENV (1<<4) against git_repository_init_options.flags, where 1<<4 is GIT_REPOSITORY_INIT_MKPATH, so MKPATH makes init's symlink probe (are_symlinks_supported, repository.c:2236) load the system/global config from the GIT_CONFIG_* environment; the parameter is GIT_UNUSED outside GIT_WIN32, so only Windows builds observe it. Rust: `OpenFlag` (#[repr(u32)], #[non_exhaustive], fallible from_raw/TryFrom, UnnamedOpenFlag) and the `OpenFlags(c_uint)` set (from_bits_retain keeps unnamed bits, bits/unnamed_bits/contains/insert/remove/iter, BitOr, FromIterator, Debug) in repository/repository.rs.

types.name: git_repository_state_t
types._comment_agent: Plain C enum, values 0..=11, no lifecycle. Its only producer is git_repository_state, which returns it as an int (or -1 when copying the gitdir path fails); reset.c compares it against MERGE/REVERT/CHERRYPICK. Wrapped as a fieldless RepositoryState, converted fallibly from a raw value; GIT_REPOSITORY_STATE_NONE is the Clean variant.

types.name: git_signature
types._comment_agent: git_signature is a heap object owned by a single holder: CBox<Signature, SignatureFree> (git_signature_free drops it with both strings; git_signature_dup deep-copies it, refusing NULL fields that C would strdup). Public consumers otherwise receive `const git_signature *` borrowed from a parent (git_commit_author/committer, git_tag_tagger, git_note_author/committer, git_reflog_entry_committer, git_blame_hunk fields) and only read it; every `const git_signature *` argument (commit/tag/note/reflog/stash/rebase creation) is only read and copied, so a caller-built struct over borrowed strings (SignatureView) is a valid argument. `when` is an embedded git_time value. No refcount, no lock. Constructors: git_signature_new, git_signature_now, git_signature_from_buffer (alloc through out-param), git_signature_default / git_signature_default_from_env (need a git_repository; left to the object/signature symbol batch). C defects: git_signature_new leaks p (and p->name) when a string allocation fails; git_signature_dup leaks the partial copy on OOM; git_signature_default_from_env frees author/committer with git__free on error, leaking their strings.

ptr.note: NUL-terminated author email; same ownership as `name`: allocated by git_signature_new / from_buffer / dup from libgit2's allocator and freed by git_signature_free with git__free; pool-borrowed only in git_transaction's internal git_signature__pdup copies. NULL after an allocation failure inside git_signature__parse (unchecked extract_trimmed), which git_signature_dup and the commit writer then dereference. Never written through.

NUL-terminated author name. Owned on every public path: git_signature_new / git_signature_from_buffer (git__substrdup via extract_trimmed) and git_signature_dup (git__strdup) allocate it from libgit2's allocator, and git_signature_free releases it with git__free (also called by git_commit__free, git_tag__free, git_reflog_entry__free, git_note_free, free_hunk on the signatures those objects own). Borrowed only in the internal git_signature__pdup copies a git_transaction keeps in its pool (transaction.c copy_common / dup_reflog), which are never freed individually and never reach a public consumer. Nullable: git_signature__parse does not check extract_trimmed's result, so an allocation failure leaves it NULL while the parse (git_signature_from_buffer, commit/tag/reflog parsing) still succeeds; refdb_reftable_log_fill checks for that, git_signature_dup (strdup(NULL)) and git_signature__writebuf (%s) do not. A calloc'd signature is NULL before parse. Never written through; libgit2 only reads, copies or frees it. Rust: Option<&CStr> getter on SignatureRef, replacement setters taking an OdbDataStr (git__malloc storage released by git__free) on SignatureMut.

types.name: git_strarray
types._comment_agent: Wrapped in core/strarray.rs (core wave 0 batch 4) as StrArray + StrArrayVal = CVal<StrArray, StrArrayDispose> for the owned form (strings move as OdbDataStrVec), and StrArrayView<'a> for the borrowed input form, which hands out StrArrayRef only. git_strarray_copy (the deep cloner) is hidden under DEPRECATE_HARD, so copies go through OdbDataStrVec::dup_all. git_strarray_dispose is skipped for a NULL `strings` (empty state; see the first-init allocator race).

ptr.note: A buffer of `count` NUL-terminated `char *` elements. Two statically distinct contracts, decided by API direction. (1) OUTPUT (git_reference_list, git_tag_list(_match), git_remote_list, git_worktree_list, git_remote_get_fetch/push_refspecs via copy_refspecs, git_remote_rename problems, GIT_OPT_GET_EXTENSIONS, store_refs): libgit2 writes `strings`/`count` without disposing what the struct held, from a git_vector (git_vector_detach / .contents, i.e. git__reallocarray storage with spare capacity) whose elements are git__strdup'd; the struct owns the array and every string, and git_strarray_dispose frees strings[0..count) then the array with git__free, then zeroes the struct. git_vector_init(&v, 8) allocates eagerly, so an empty result is often a NON-NULL array with count 0 (refs.c, tag.c, remote.c, repository.c extensions); worktree.c and the error paths leave NULL/0. Producers never store a NULL element. (2) INPUT (`const git_strarray *` args: git_index_add_all/remove_all/update_all, git_remote_fetch/push/upload/download/connect, git_reset_default, git_pathspec_new, git_stash_save_with_opts, and by-value option fields: git_diff_options.pathspec, git_checkout_options.paths, custom_headers, remote_push_options): libgit2 only reads strings[0..count) (pathspec/iterator/headers deref every element, so NULL elements are invalid), copies what it keeps (git_strarray_copy, git__strdup), and never frees or writes the caller's array: borrowed for the call / the options' lifetime. git_remote_connect memcpys the caller's struct into its options and copies it via git_remote_connect_options_dup before use. NULL `strings` means empty only with count 0; git_strarray_dispose with NULL strings and count > 0 derefs NULL. Owned arrays are written (dispose zeroes, producers fill), borrowed ones are const.

types.name: git_submodule_ignore_t
types._comment_agent: Values -1 (UNSPECIFIED), 1 NONE, 2 UNTRACKED, 3 DIRTY, 4 ALL; 0 is unnamed (the old GIT_SUBMODULE_IGNORE_DEFAULT the types.h comment still mentions is gone). Consumers: git_submodule_status / git_submodule__status read UNSPECIFIED as 'the submodule's configured value' and compare the rest for equality (any other value behaves like UNTRACKED). git_diff_options.ignore_submodules: `<= 0` (0 from a zeroed struct, or UNSPECIFIED from GIT_DIFF_OPTIONS_INIT) means 'read diff.ignoreSubmodules' (diff_generate.c:561). git_submodule_set_ignore maps through _sm_ignore_map, so UNSPECIFIED, 0 and anything outside 1..4 fail with GIT_ERROR_SUBMODULE 'invalid value for ignore'. Producers (git_submodule_ignore, git_submodule_parse_ignore from config strings none/untracked/dirty/all/true/false) only return 1..4, plus UNSPECIFIED from git_submodule_ignore(NULL) via GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL. Wrapped as core::types::SubmoduleIgnore (repr(i32)), converted fallibly with from_raw.

types.name: git_submodule_recurse_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_SUBMODULE_RECURSE_NO = 0, _YES = 1, _ONDEMAND = 2, include/git2/types.h; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle: passed and returned by value. Producers: submodule_parse_recurse (submodule.c:2034) maps .gitmodules/config fetchRecurseSubmodules through _sm_recurse_map (bool false->NO, true->YES, 'on-demand' case-insensitive->ONDEMAND); an unreadable spelling writes YES to *out then fails git_submodule_lookup with GIT_EINVALID 'invalid value for submodule 'recurse' property: '<v>''; an unset setting leaves the alloc default NO (submodule.c:1962). git_submodule_fetch_recurse_submodules returns sm->fetch_recurse unchanged (only named values; NULL sm -> GIT_ASSERT_ARG, NO in release, abort in the Debug/coverage build). Consumer: git_submodule_set_fetch_recurse_submodules -> write_mapped_var -> git_config_lookup_map_enum: unnamed values fail -1 GIT_ERROR_SUBMODULE 'invalid value for fetchRecurseSubmodules'; YES writes 'true', ONDEMAND 'on-demand', NO (CONFIGMAP_FALSE, str NULL) DELETES the .gitmodules key and so fails GIT_ENOTFOUND (GIT_ERROR_CONFIG 'could not find key 'submodule.<name>.fetchRecurseSubmodules' to delete') when the key is absent, although the submodule already reads NO. Rust: SubmoduleRecurse in core/types.rs, converted fallibly (from_raw/TryFrom -> UnnamedSubmoduleRecurse), Default = No (unset). The submodule symbol batch should treat that ENOTFOUND as success or pre-check, and route returned values through from_raw.

types.name: git_submodule_update_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_SUBMODULE_UPDATE_CHECKOUT = 1, _REBASE = 2, _MERGE = 3, _NONE = 4, _DEFAULT = 0, include/git2/types.h; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle: passed and returned by value. DEFAULT (0) is never produced and never accepted: git_submodule_parse_update (submodule.c:2020) maps only via _sm_update_map ('checkout','rebase','merge','none' case-insensitive, bool true->CHECKOUT, false->NONE; an unreadable spelling writes CHECKOUT to *out and fails git_submodule_lookup with GIT_EINVALID 'invalid value for submodule 'update' property: '<v>''), an unset setting keeps the alloc default CHECKOUT (submodule.c:1961), git_submodule_update_strategy maps any value < CHECKOUT to CHECKOUT (NULL sm -> GIT_ASSERT_ARG, NONE in release, abort in Debug), and git_submodule_set_update -> write_mapped_var refuses 0 and every other unnamed value with -1 GIT_ERROR_SUBMODULE 'invalid value for update'; named values are written to .gitmodules by name ('checkout','rebase','merge','none'). git_submodule_init writes submodule.<name>.update into .git/config via submodule_update_to_str for every value but CHECKOUT (whose entry it removes); its NULL return is unreachable. The header's GIT_SUBMODULE_UPDATE_RESET does not exist. Rust: SubmoduleUpdate in core/types.rs has no variant for DEFAULT (from_raw(0) = None, UnnamedSubmoduleUpdate), Default = Checkout so from_raw(raw).unwrap_or_default() resolves 0 as C does; typed setters can then never send a value C refuses.

types.name: git_time
types._comment_agent: Plain resource-free value (int64 seconds, int offset in minutes, char sign); no pointer field, no lifecycle routine: held by value (embedded in git_signature.when, copied field-wise by git_signature_dup/__pdup) and never released. git_signature_new sets sign = offset < 0 ? '-' : '+'. git_signature__parse leaves a calloc'd 0 sign/offset without a timezone, stores tz_start[0] verbatim as sign (any byte, not only '+'/'-') with offset 0 for a malformed timezone, and keeps the zeroes when hours > 14 or mins > 59. git_signature__writebuf (the one writer: commit, tag and reflog creation) prints '-' when offset < 0 or sign == '-' (the '-0000' case), '+' otherwise, hours/minutes from |offset| with %02d%02d, and the SECONDS THROUGH `(unsigned)sig->when.time` (%u): a time before the epoch or past 2106 is written wrapped modulo 2^32; it negates a negative offset as an int, so offset == INT_MIN overflows (C UB; the UBSan build aborts) - wrappers of the writing routines must refuse or document such a Time (core review wave 0, 2026-10-09; tests/equiv/types.rs::signature_zones_are_written_from_offset_and_sign). git_signature__equal compares the three fields. All-zero is a valid value. Wrapped as Time/TimeRef/TimeMut in core/types.rs (CZeroable, Copy, Send/Sync).

types.name: git_trace_level_t
types._comment_agent: C enum, values 0..6 (NONE..TRACE), passed by value. Consumers: git_trace_set stores any value in git_trace__data.level (GIT_ASSERT_ARG level == 0 || callback != NULL, an abort in Debug builds); git_trace() emits when git_trace__data.level >= level, so the integer order is the verbosity order; internal emitters only pass named levels (INFO/DEBUG/TRACE) to git_trace_cb. Wrapped as the fieldless TraceLevel enum (repr u32, Ord over the C values) with a fallible from_raw in core/trace.rs.

types.name: git_worktree
types._comment_agent: git_worktree is opaque in the public API (forward-declared in git2/types.h); its body is private to src/libgit2/worktree.h and only worktree.c, repository.c (git_repository_open_from_worktree) and submodule.c (get_url_base) read fields. Sole owner, no refcount, no lock, no copy routine: CBox<Worktree, WorktreeFree> with git_worktree_free (frees six strings then the struct, NULL is a no-op). Constructors, all alloc through an out-param and all needing a git_repository: git_worktree_lookup (sets *out NULL first), git_worktree_open_from_repository (does NOT reset *out on failure and has no GIT_ASSERT_ARG on repo), git_worktree_add (needs git_worktree_add_options). Every string is copied (strdup / read from the worktree's files / prettified), so a worktree never borrows the repository it was looked up in and may outlive it. Only git_worktree_lock / git_worktree_unlock write through the struct (the `locked` bit, which nothing reads back); every other consumer reads.

ptr.note: Parent repository's common dir, read from `<gitdir>/commondir` by git_worktree__read_link. Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

Prettified path of `<commondir>/worktrees/<name>/`, detached from a git_str. Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

Path of the working tree's `.git` file, read from `<gitdir>/gitdir` by git_worktree__read_link (made absolute against the gitdir when relative). Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

Worktree name: git__strdup of the lookup name, or git_fs_path_basename of the worktree repo's gitdir in open_from_repository; returned borrowed by git_worktree_name. Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

Parent working directory: git__strdup of git_repository_workdir(repo) in git_worktree_lookup (NULL when the repository is bare) or of the prettified `<commondir>/..` in open_from_repository. git_worktree_validate and get_url_base check it for NULL. Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

Working directory: git_fs_path_dirname(gitlink_path); returned borrowed by git_worktree_path. Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

types.name: git_worktree_add_options
