types._comment_agent: Caller-built by-value options (stack in C), filled by git_worktree_add_options_init / GIT_WORKTREE_ADD_OPTIONS_INIT, never allocated or freed by libgit2; git_worktree_add (the only consumer) refuses version 0 or >1 via GIT_ERROR_CHECK_VERSION, memcpys it, reads lock and checkout_existing as C booleans (nonzero), dups ref, and copies checkout_options by value into git_checkout_head. No release, dispose or clone primitive; the embedded git_checkout_options borrows its own strings/paths/index/payloads. Review (wave 1 type review): a failing checkout through the embedded checkout_options (e.g. target_directory naming an existing file: git_checkout_head fails GIT_EEXISTS 'failed to make directory ...: directory exists') happens AFTER git_worktree_add has written worktrees/<name>/{commondir,gitdir,HEAD,refs/} and <wt>/.git and run git_refdb_init, so it leaves a lookup-able, never checked-out worktree whose HEAD holds the branch checked out; *out stays NULL and a retry of the same name fails 'reference ... is already checked out' (-1). The same for any later failure (git_repository_open, git_worktree_lookup); a failed git_futils_mkdir(worktree) (path exists / parent missing) leaves only the admin dir, which makes a retry GIT_EEXISTS.

ptr.note: The caller's attached reference, borrowed for the git_worktree_add call: git_worktree_add memcpys the options, tests git_reference_is_branch (name only), then git_reference_dup's it (reads name/target/peel, bumps the refdb count, never writes the reference) and frees only its own copy. NULL means 'branch named after the worktree' (checkout_existing) or a new branch at HEAD. Must be attached: dup copies ->db, and git_branch_is_checked_out reaches db->repo, so an unattached reference (NULL db) crashes and a reference outliving its repository reads a freed repo. git_worktree_add_options_init writes NULL; nothing frees it.

types.name: git_worktree_prune_options
types._comment_agent: Resource-free POD of two 32-bit scalars (8 bytes, no padding, no pointer). No dropper, disposer or cloner: callers hold it by value (stack) and C copies it by value. Its one lifecycle primitive is the in-place init constructor git_worktree_prune_options_init(opts, version), which memcpys GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_OPTIONS_INIT = {1, 0} and fails (git_error_set GIT_ERROR_INVALID, opts untouched) only for version 0 or > GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_OPTIONS_VERSION. All-zero is NOT the default: consumers (git_worktree_is_prunable, git_worktree_prune) reject version 0 with -1 'invalid version 0 on git_worktree_prune_options'. Consumers take it nullable and read-only (version check, then memcpy into a local); flags bits outside git_worktree_prune_t are ignored. Not shared with threads by C; no lock.

types.name: git_worktree_prune_t
types._comment_agent: Flag enum: VALID=1<<0, LOCKED=1<<1, WORKING_TREE=1<<2, OR-ed into git_worktree_prune_options.flags (uint32_t). C tests each bit with & and ignores the others, so any u32 is a valid flags value; the enum names single bits only.

types.name: git_writestream
types._comment_agent: git_writestream is a vtable header embedded as the first member of a concrete stream (blob_writestream, buffered_stream, buf_stream, checkout_stream, user filter streams); its three members take the header pointer and cast it back to the container, so a header is never valid detached from its container (never copied or held by value). Ownership: git_blob_create_from_stream returns an owned stream (released by its own `free`, or consumed by git_blob_create_from_stream_commit); git_filter_list_stream_{buffer,file,blob} borrow a caller target for the call and write/close (never free) it; a user filter's git_filter_stream_fn returns an owned stream to libgit2, which frees it with its `free` member after closing the chain, and gets `next` borrowed for the chain's life. Rust wrapper: WriteStream/WriteStreamRef/WriteStreamMut (core/types.rs), WriteStreamBox = CBox<WriteStream, WriteStreamFree> (free through the object's own member), RustWriteStream<W: StreamWriter> for Rust implementations.

ptr.note: Function pointer, set once at construction, never NULL. Finishes the stream; afterwards only `free` is valid (buf_stream/checkout_stream GIT_ASSERT on a second close, buffered_stream reruns its filter and closes its target again, blob close zeroes the filebuf so commit/write call a NULL fn). git_filter_list_stream_* call it exactly once on the head of the chain, and each buffered stream closes its target once; the user-supplied target is closed but never freed by libgit2. git_blob_create_from_stream documents that its stream must not be closed by the caller (commit flushes the filebuf close discarded).

Function pointer, set once at construction, never NULL: the stream's own destructor, releasing the CONTAINING object (blob_writestream_free: filebuf cleanup + git__free(hintpath) + git__free(stream); buffered_stream_free: disposes its bufs + git__free; buf_stream_free / checkout_stream_free: no-op for stack streams). It is the type's dropper, recoverable from the object, so the Rust release strategy (WriteStreamFree) is stateless. Valid after close or without close. libgit2 frees the streams it creates (filter_streams_free) and a user filter's stream returned through git_filter_stream_fn, never the caller's target; git_blob_create_from_stream_commit frees its argument.

Function pointer (code, static lifetime), set once by every producer at construction (blob_writestream_write, buffered_stream_write, buf_stream_write, checkout_stream_write) and never rewritten; never NULL. Called as stream->write(stream, buf, len) with `stream` = the header itself, which each implementation casts back to its container struct (git_writestream is the first member `parent`/`base`), so the member is only valid for the object it was read from. `< 0` is failure (callers test `< 0`; buffered_stream_close tests `== 0`). Calling it after `close` is invalid: blob streams then call a NULL filebuf write fn (git_filebuf_cleanup zeroes the filebuf), checkout streams write to a closed (possibly reused) fd, buf_stream fails GIT_ASSERT (abort in Debug builds).

The blob_writestream header (cast back to its container), released with its filebuf and hintpath; installed as git_writestream.free by git_blob_create_from_stream, and called by git_blob_create_from_stream_commit and on its own error path.

The buffered_stream header (cast back to its container); disposes input/temp_buf and git__frees the container, leaving the target alone. Installed as git_writestream.free; called by filter_streams_free.
libc calloc: ZEROING; NULL on overflow or failure. Released by free.
libc free: releases malloc/calloc/realloc storage; NULL is a no-op.
git__malloc(nelem*elsize) then memset 0: ZEROING; NULL on multiplication overflow (no error set) or OOM. Internal; released by git__free.

git__allocator.gfree(ptr): releases any git__malloc-family storage without reading it; NULL is a no-op (stdalloc free, failalloc no-op). Internal; publicly reachable only through git_odb_backend_data_free.

git__allocator.gmalloc(len): NON-zeroing; NULL on OOM with git_error_set_oom; always NULL before git_libgit2_init (failalloc). Internal (hidden visibility); publicly reachable only through git_odb_backend_data_alloc. Released by git__free.
git__reallocarray(NULL, nelem, elsize): NON-zeroing array storage; NULL on overflow or OOM. Internal; released by git__free.
Read for strlen(str)+1 bytes during the call only; NULL is dereferenced (crash), so not nullable.

Fresh git__malloc(strlen(str)+1) storage holding a copy of str with its terminator: the NUL-terminated string cloner behind git_strarray_copy, git_signature_new/dup and most libgit2 string fields. NULL on OOM (git_error_set_oom via git__malloc; before git_libgit2_init every request fails). Internal (hidden visibility): Rust reproduces it as OdbDataStrFree::dup / str_dup over git_odb_backend_data_alloc; released by git__free, publicly git_odb_backend_data_free.
Read for p_strnlen(str, n) bytes during the call only: a NUL within the first n bytes ends the copy, so the input may be an unterminated run of n bytes.

Fresh git__malloc(len+1) storage holding the first len = strnlen(str, n) bytes of str plus a terminator: a bounded string cloner. NULL on OOM. Internal; released by git__free (publicly git_odb_backend_data_free).
Read for exactly n bytes during the call only, NUL or not: the caller bounds the run (a path component, a token).

Fresh git__malloc(n+1) storage holding the n bytes at str plus a terminator: a byte-run-to-string cloner. NULL on OOM or when n+1 overflows to 0 only through malloc(0) semantics (no overflow check). Internal; released by git__free (publicly git_odb_backend_data_free).
Consumes the object: NULL is a no-op; REAL frees commit/tree/strings, VIRTUAL frees index/parents, any other type aborts; then git__free of the struct. Never touches the repository.
NUL-terminated string read for the call and copied (git__strdup), never retained
object id, read for the call (git_commit_lookup); any type byte reaches C

Out slot: receives a fresh REAL annotated commit (git__calloc'd) owned by the caller, released by git_annotated_commit_free. Written by the lookup on success; then two git__strdup calls (branch_name, remote_url) — if either fails it returns -1 with *out STILL SET, so the caller must free it. A failed lookup returns -1, not its code.

repository, borrowed for the call: commit lookup through its odb and object cache; not retained by the annotated commit itself (its commit object keeps an unowned back-pointer).

Out-slot (GIT_ASSERT_ARG): on success receives a fresh git__calloc'd blob_writestream header, owned by the caller and released by its own `free` member or consumed by git_blob_create_from_stream_commit; untouched on failure.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; stored unretained in the stream (stream->repo), which commit later uses: the repository must outlive the stream.

Must be a stream from git_blob_create_from_stream (cast to blob_writestream unchecked) that was never closed (close zeroes the filebuf; the flush then calls a NULL write fn). Consumed on every path: blob_writestream_free runs on success and failure.
Out-parameter: the new blob's id, written on success only (git_blob__create_from_paths).

The caller's git_buf, held by value (stack or embedded); NULL is a no-op. Frees buf->ptr with git__free unless it is the static git_str__initstr (NULL included), then resets the struct to {git_str__initstr, 0, 0}: reusable, never freed itself.

The caller's storage, borrowed for the call; written whole (memcpy of GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_INIT: version 1, every other field zero/NULL) and only when `version` is 1. For version 0 or > 1 it returns -1 with GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'invalid version N on git_checkout_options' and leaves *opts untouched (still uninitialised if it was). Not NULL-checked: NULL with version 1 is a NULL write. With version 1 it reaches no global, allocator or thread state, so it needs no runtime pin.

The caller's git_commitarray, borrowed for the call: NULL is a no-op; otherwise git_commit_free on each of the first count commits, git__free(commits), then memset to {NULL, 0}, so a second dispose is harmless. The struct itself is not freed (held inline). Accepts {NULL, 0} (git__free(NULL), which reads git__allocator: the Rust policy skips it); a NULL commits with count > 0 dereferences NULL. Wrapped as CommitArrayDispose (object/commit.rs).

Releases one reference (NULL is a no-op): GIT_REFCOUNT_DEC frees the config (config_free: down-ref each backend instance, which frees its backend at 0; dispose both vectors; git__free) once the atomic count reaches 0 and no repository owns it (rc.owner NULL); a repository-owned config at 0 is freed by the repository's set_config(NULL). Wrapped as the drop of ConfigFree (config/config.rs), behind ConfigBox and ConfigArc.

Out slot, written only on success with a fresh git__calloc'd config (empty readers/writers vectors, refcount 1, no owner): the caller's only reference, released by git_config_free. Untouched on failure (OOM, returns -1). Pre-init the calloc goes through failalloc and git_error_set_oom writes through an invalid TLS key, so the wrapper pins the runtime first. Wrapped as ConfigFree's CNew and Config::new (config/config.rs).
Releases a git_error_save copy (message, then the struct, with git__free); NULL and the static errors are ignored. Internal (hidden).

Never NULL. Points at one of four static errors (uninitialized_error before git_libgit2_init / after the last shutdown, tlsdata_error when the thread state cannot be allocated, no_error, oom_error) or at the calling thread's error_threadstate.error, whose message aliases the thread's git_str buffer; the next git_error_set*/git_error_clear on that thread (any failing libgit2 call) rewrites it and may reallocate the message, and thread exit or the last git_libgit2_shutdown frees it. Borrow valid only until the next libgit2 call on the thread: copy out (ErrorBuf). Caller must not free.

Consumes a git_error_save result: makes it the thread's last error (a static one by pointer, a copy by re-setting its class and message) and then releases it with git_error_free. NULL is rejected (GIT_ASSERT_ARG). Internal (hidden).

Out slot. Receives either a fresh git__malloc copy of the thread's last error (message git__strdup'ed), owned by the caller and released by git_error_free / git_error_restore, or one of the static errors (no_error, oom_error, tlsdata_error, or the static last error itself), which those routines skip (IS_STATIC_ERROR). Leaks the copy when the message strdup fails. Internal (src/util/errors.h, hidden).

printf-style format read during the call only (git_str_vprintf into the thread's error buffer), together with the variadic arguments it names; never retained. NULL is accepted: the message is then empty, or for GIT_ERROR_OS just strerror(errno). With GIT_ERROR_OS and a non-NULL fmt, ': ' and strerror(errno) are appended when errno != 0, and errno is reset to 0. Allocation failure leaves `last` at the static oom_error (git__realloc -> git_error_set_oom) and the thread's buffer stuck at git_str__oom, so later messages on that thread are dropped. Like every errors.c entry point, it reads TLS under errors.c's tls_key, which only exists while the runtime is initialised (pre-init it reads key 0's foreign block). Safe Rust passes "%s" with a &CStr message, or NULL (set_without_message).

Copied with git_str_puts into the thread's error buffer during the call; never retained (the header's 'static string' wording is wrong: any string works). NULL is rejected by GIT_ASSERT_ARG: -1 and an 'invalid argument' error in release builds, assert() abort under _DEBUG/GIT_ASSERT_HARD (the coverage build). Returns -1 when the thread state cannot be allocated or the copy runs out of memory (buffer then stuck at git_str__oom, `last` at oom_error), 0 otherwise; unlike git_error_set it never consults errno.

Releases one counted reference: NULL is a no-op; GIT_REFCOUNT_DEC frees through index_free (clears entries, names, reuc, extensions, deleted, the entry map, index_file_path, then git__free on the zeroed struct) once the count reaches 0 while rc.owner is NULL. Every reference handed out by git_index_open/open_ext/new/new_ext, git_repository_index, git_rebase_inmemory_index and the merge/cherrypick/revert/apply index results is released here; the repository releases its own through set_index. Rust: the c_drop of IndexFree for both CBox<Index> (sole reference) and CArc<Index> (shared counted reference).

Out slot (GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL). On success it receives a fresh calloc-ed in-memory index holding the only reference (refcount 1, no owner, index_file_path NULL), which the caller releases with git_index_free; on failure (OOM) it is left untouched. Rust: Index::new -> IndexBox, and the CNew of IndexFree.
Options, only read for the call (version checked by GIT_ERROR_CHECK_VERSION; oid_type 0 = GIT_OID_DEFAULT, otherwise GIT_ASSERT_ARG(git_oid_type_is_valid), an abort in Debug builds). NULL = defaults.
As git_index_new: a fresh in-memory index holding the only reference, released with git_index_free; untouched on failure.

Out slot (GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL). On success it receives a fresh index backed by index_path, holding the only reference (refcount 1, no owner), read from disk when the file exists; released with git_index_free. Left untouched on failure: the half-built index is freed (git_pool_clear + git_index_free on refcount 0), except that read_entry leaks the decompressed path of a version 4 entry running past the buffer. Rust: Index::open -> IndexBox.

Path of the index file, read for the call and git__strdup-ed, never retained. NULL makes it git_index_new (an in-memory index); a nonexistent path gives an empty index that is not on disk; a directory or an unreadable/corrupt file fails (-1). An empty path is accepted, but git_index_write on that index memcpys from a NULL path_original in git_filebuf_open_withsize (UB); Rust takes &CStr and refuses the empty string.
As git_index_open: a fresh index holding the only reference, released with git_index_free; untouched on failure (the half-built index is freed).
Index file path, read and git__strdup-ed, never retained; NULL = in-memory index; an empty path is accepted but its write is UB (see git_index_open).
Options, only read for the call (version checked; oid_type 0 = GIT_OID_DEFAULT, otherwise GIT_ASSERT_ARG(git_oid_type_is_valid), an abort in Debug builds). NULL = defaults.

Returns the GIT_BUILD_CPU / GIT_BUILD_COMMIT string literal (cmake-configured in git2_features.h) or NULL for any other key or an unrecorded item; never freed, valid while libgit2.so is loaded. Touches no runtime state, so needs no git_libgit2_init.

Returns a string literal naming the compiled-in backend of the feature, or NULL for an unnamed value, a feature not compiled in, or GIT_FEATURE_HTTP (no backend selection). The GIT_ASSERT_WITH_RETVAL paths (a compiled-in feature whose backend define CMake did not set) are unreachable for any CMake-configured build; in release they would git_error_set (pre-init TLS hazard), in Debug they abort. Never freed; needs no git_libgit2_init.
LIBGIT2_VERSION_PRERELEASE string literal in libgit2.so's rodata ("alpha", "beta", "rcN"), or NULL for a final release. Never freed; needs no initialisation.
Out-param, written unconditionally with LIBGIT2_VERSION_MAJOR; NULL dereferenced.
Out-param, written unconditionally with LIBGIT2_VERSION_MINOR; NULL dereferenced.
Out-param, written unconditionally with LIBGIT2_VERSION_REVISION; NULL dereferenced. Always returns 0; needs no initialisation.
GIT_UNUSED(backend): never read or written, so NULL is accepted on observed behaviour; the header documents it as the allocating backend. Rust policies pass NULL.

git__malloc(len): plain, NON-zeroing storage from git__allocator.gmalloc (stdalloc malloc by default). NULL on OOM via git_error_set_oom. HAZARD: before git_libgit2_init (and after the last shutdown) failalloc makes every request fail, and git_error_set_oom then reads the error TLS slot under an uninitialised/deleted key (0), writing &oom_error into another component's TLS block (ASan: unknown-crash in git_error_set_oom, errors.c:170). Rust strategies pin the runtime with their own git_libgit2_init reference first. len 0 is malloc(0): implementation-defined NULL or a unique pointer. Released by git_odb_backend_data_free or, once returned from a backend read callback, by libgit2's own git__free. Holds one object, a byte buffer, or - filled with a copy and its terminator, as git__strdup does (git__strdup is not exported) - a NUL-terminated string that git_strarray_dispose / git_signature_free / git_buf_dispose may release; Rust OdbDataStrFree::dup, OdbDataStrVec::dup_all and their Clone build strings and char** arrays through it.
GIT_UNUSED(backend): never read or written, so NULL is accepted on observed behaviour.

git__free(data) -> git__allocator.gfree: releases any git__malloc/git__calloc/git__realloc storage (an object, a buffer, or a NUL-terminated string) without reading it; NULL is a no-op. Strings: libgit2 makes its strings with git__strdup/git__strndup/git__substrdup (git__malloc) and releases them with git__free in git_strarray_dispose (each element, then the array), git_signature_free (name, email) and git_buf_dispose (ptr), none of which exports a single-string free, so this is the only exported releaser for one libgit2 string or a char** array of them; Rust OdbDataStrFree / OdbDataStrVec drop through it. Frees through the CURRENT allocator, so storage must not outlive a GIT_OPT_SET_ALLOCATOR swap.

A refcount down-ref (GIT_REFCOUNT_DEC): NULL is a no-op; the atomic count drops by one, and odb_free runs only when it reaches 0 while no repository owns the odb (rc.owner NULL): every backend's own free, the commit-graph, the backend vector, own_cache, the mutex, then git__free. Callable from any thread. libgit2 exports no matching up-ref; git_repository_odb returns a +1 reference to a repository's odb, which this releases.

Out slot: on success receives a fresh git__calloc'd odb holding one reference (no backends, own cache, mutex), owned by the caller and released by git_odb_free; left untouched on failure (OOM in the calloc, mutex, cache or vector init, each unwound without leaks). Equivalent to git_odb_new_ext(out, NULL): SHA-1 ids.

NULL selects the defaults; otherwise version-checked (GIT_ERROR_CHECK_VERSION) and memcpy'd into db->options, never retained. oid_type 0 becomes GIT_OID_DEFAULT; any other value is stored unvalidated (an unnamed one later breaks hashing and git_repository_wrap_odb's GIT_ASSERT).

Out slot: on success receives a fresh git__calloc'd odb holding one reference (no backends, own cache, mutex), owned by the caller and released by git_odb_free; left untouched on failure (OOM in the calloc, mutex, cache or vector init, each unwound without leaks).

GIT_ASSERT_ARG; stat'ed and copied into the loose/pack backends' paths and the alternates walk, never retained. A path that cannot be stat'ed fails GIT_ERROR_ODB "failed to load object database in '<dir>'"; a regular file opens (its backends then fail every write); an unreadable info/alternates fails the open.

Out slot: set to NULL first, then receives a fresh odb (one reference) with the loose and pack backends for objects_dir, its commit-graph and alternates (alternates files read at depths 0..5, so directories six levels deep; a directory already open by inode is skipped, a missing alternate ignored); released by git_odb_free. On failure the half-built odb is freed with git_odb_free and the slot stays NULL; a failing add_backend_internal (OOM) leaks the backend just created. Equivalent to git_odb_open_ext(out, objects_dir, NULL).

GIT_ASSERT_ARG; stat'ed and copied into the loose/pack backends' paths and the alternates walk, never retained. A path that cannot be stat'ed fails GIT_ERROR_ODB "failed to load object database in '<dir>'"; a regular file opens (its backends then fail every write); an unreadable info/alternates fails the open.

NULL selects the defaults; otherwise version-checked (GIT_ERROR_CHECK_VERSION) and memcpy'd into db->options, never retained. oid_type 0 becomes GIT_OID_DEFAULT; any other value is stored unvalidated (an unnamed one later breaks hashing and git_repository_wrap_odb's GIT_ASSERT).

Out slot: set to NULL first, then receives a fresh odb (one reference) with the loose and pack backends for objects_dir, its commit-graph and alternates (alternates files read at depths 0..5, so directories six levels deep; a directory already open by inode is skipped, a missing alternate ignored); released by git_odb_free. On failure the half-built odb is freed with git_odb_free and the slot stays NULL; a failing add_backend_internal (OOM) leaks the backend just created.
memcmp over the whole sizeof(git_oid) (type byte first, then all 32 id bytes); read for the call only. Any byte pattern is accepted; may alias b.
As a; may alias a.
memcpy destination, the whole sizeof(git_oid); must not overlap src.
memcpy source, read for the call only; must not overlap out (memcpy).
memcmp over the whole git_oid, == 0; read for the call only; may alias b.
As a.
Type selects the hex size; unknown type -> GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'unable to parse OID - unknown type', -1, nothing written (sets the thread error, so the runtime must be initialised).
Caller buffer of at least git_oid_hexsize(type) bytes (40/64); exactly that many hex digits written, no NUL. Untouched when the type is unknown.
Caller storage filled in place after the length/type checks (memset then nibbles); partially written when a later character is invalid. Never retained.

Counted run of `len` hex characters, not NUL-terminated; read only after the type and 1 <= len <= hexsize checks, stopping at the first non-hex one. GIT_ASSERT_ARG(str) (abort in _DEBUG builds) rejects NULL.
Caller storage filled in place (memset, type, memcpy of git_oid_size(type) bytes); untouched when the type is unknown.
Exactly git_oid_size(type) bytes are read (20 for SHA1, 32 for SHA256) with no length argument: the caller must supply that many. Not read for an unknown type.
Caller storage filled in place: from_prefix memsets it and sets type and id; on failure it may be left partially written (zeroed + some nibbles). Never retained.
NUL-terminated hex text read for the call only: hexsize chars, stopping at the first non-hex one (NUL included), then str[hexsize] only once all hexsize were hex, so any C string is read in bounds.
Reads the 32 id bytes only (memcmp against a zero array); the type byte is ignored.

Types compared first (returns their difference); then the first len hex digits of id, len capped at GIT_OID_MAX_HEXSIZE so at most 32 bytes are read. Returns 0 on match, 1 or the type difference otherwise (not an ordering).
As oid_a.
NULL is accepted (zero-fills str). Unknown type -> -1 with GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'unable to parse OID - unknown type'.

Counted buffer of n bytes: the first min(n, hexsize) are hex digits, the rest (when n > hexsize) zeroed; no NUL added otherwise. With oid NULL all n bytes are zeroed. Untouched when the type is unknown.
Unknown type -> -1 with GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'unable to parse OID - unknown type'.
Caller buffer of at least hexsize + 1 bytes (41/65): two digits, '/', the remaining hexsize - 2 digits; no NUL. Untouched when the type is unknown.

Mutated in place (trie grown via resize_trie/push_leaf, min_length raised, `full` set at SHRT_MAX nodes). Dereferenced unconditionally. After a failed resize nodes is NULL and a further add crashes. The failed resize (OOM, GIT_ERROR_NOMEMORY) is the only way into the NULL-nodes state; 'OID set full' leaves the trie intact and every later add fails early.

RETAINED: push_leaf stores &text_oid[i+1] as a leaf tail that later adds read, so the string must outlive the shortener (despite the header's 'owned by the user'). NULL returns min_length without reading. Only the characters walked are validated: a short or non-hex id is stored as a tail whose first char later gives git__fromhex == -1, and push_leaf then writes node->children[-1], corrupting the preceding trie node without any sanitizer report. Callers must pass full 40-char hex ids. Only text_oid[0..40) is ever read (the walk stops at i < GIT_OID_SHA1_HEXSIZE and a leaf at depth d holds &text[d], converted only at d <= 39), so no NUL is needed once 40 hex bytes are present; a stored tail may be the one-past pointer &text[40], never dereferenced.
Frees nodes then the shortener (git__free); NULL is a no-op. Does not touch the borrowed text ids its leaves point at. Safe even after a failed add left nodes NULL.

Fresh git__calloc'd shortener with a 16-node zeroed trie, node_count 1; released by git_oid_shorten_free. NULL on allocation failure, or when min_length does not round-trip through int (GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL: error set in release builds, assert(3) abort in _DEBUG builds).
Reads up to git_oid_size(type) id bytes; an unknown type has size 0, so every string compares equal.

NUL-terminated hex, read two digits per id byte until its NUL or the oid's size; an odd last digit is compared as the high nibble with a zero low nibble. Returns -1 at a non-hex digit it reads, which is indistinguishable from a byte difference of -1; characters past the id's size are never read.
As git_oid_strcmp.
As git_oid_strcmp: 0 when strcmp is 0 (so a prefix, or the empty string, matches), -1 otherwise.
NULL formats as "" (out[0] = NUL). Unknown type: empty string plus the 'unknown type' thread error.
Counted buffer of n bytes: min(n - 1, hexsize) digits then a NUL. NULL or n == 0 returns a static "" without writing. An unknown type writes only out[0] = NUL (nfmt's error is set and ignored).
Returns out itself, NUL-terminated within n, or the static string literal "" (must not be written) when out is NULL or n is 0.

Formatted with nfmt into the thread buffer; an unknown type makes nfmt fail WITHOUT writing, and the stale buffer (uninitialised and unterminated on the thread's first call: ASan heap-buffer-overflow in strlen) is returned anyway, with the 'unknown type' error set.

Per-thread buffer of GIT_OID_MAX_HEXSIZE + 1 bytes under thread_str_key, git__malloc'd on the thread's first call (NULL + OOM error on failure). Owned by libgit2: overwritten by the next git_oid_tostr_s on the same thread (also called internally by checkout/refs/odb code), freed at thread exit or by the shutdown hook. Copy it out before any other libgit2 call.

The caller's git_oidarray, borrowed for the call: its ids buffer is released with git__free, the struct itself is not (the caller holds it inline). Dereferenced unconditionally, so NULL crashes. The fields are left as they were: ids dangles afterwards, so the struct must not be read or disposed again without reinitialising it. Accepts {NULL, 0} and any ids from libgit2's allocator.

A path component read for the call. The HFS+ rules honour pathlen; the NTFS rules (GENERIC included) ignore it beyond `len >= filelen` and read name[0..8] and onward to a NUL or ':' (ntfs_end_of_filename), so the pointer must be NUL-terminated: the safe wrapper takes &CStr and passes its full length. With named gitfile/fs it never touches the error state or allocates (no runtime pin needed, safe pre-init); unnamed values give -1 GIT_ERROR_OS.

Down-ref (GIT_REFCOUNT_DEC); NULL is a no-op. Frees (backend->free, memzero, git__free) only when the count reaches 0 and no repository owns the refdb; an owned one is freed when its repository lets go. Releases exactly the caller's reference, whether from git_refdb_new/open or git_repository_refdb.

Out slot, written only on success: a fresh git__calloc'd refdb with one reference and NO backend, owned by the caller (git_refdb_free); unusable until git_refdb_set_backend succeeds (every backend routine dereferences NULL; git_refdb_compress segfaults). GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL.
Stored as db->repo without a reference: must outlive the refdb.

Out slot, written NULL first; receives a fresh refdb with one reference and the backend repo->refdb_type names (files or reftable), owned by the caller (git_refdb_free). Stays NULL on failure (backend setup failure, unknown storage format: GIT_EINVALID). GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL.
Retained without a reference by the refdb (db->repo) and its backend: must outlive the refdb. GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL.
Copied into the struct's flexible name array (strlen + memcpy); not validated. NULL is asserted on.
Copied into target.oid; its type also types a cleared peel. NULL is asserted on.
Copied into peel when non-NULL; NULL leaves peel zeroed with the target's oid type.
A fresh direct reference, DETACHED (db NULL) until a refdb attaches it; released by git_reference_free. NULL on allocation failure (error set) or a NULL argument.
Copied into the struct's flexible name array; not validated. NULL is asserted on.
git__strdup'd into target.symbolic. NULL is asserted on.

A fresh symbolic reference, DETACHED (db NULL) until a refdb attaches it; released by git_reference_free. NULL on allocation failure (the struct is freed when the target copy fails) or a NULL argument.

Out slot, always written: a fresh copy (git_reference__alloc / __alloc_symbolic of the source's name and target, peel copied) owned by the caller and released by git_reference_free, or NULL with -1 and an out-of-memory error. The copy shares the source's refdb through its own counted reference.

Read for the call (name, type, target, peel); its db's refcount is incremented through it (GIT_REFCOUNT_INC(source->db)), so a detached reference (db NULL, from git_reference__alloc*) crashes it. NULL source is dereferenced (no check).

Releases the reference: git__free(target.symbolic) for a symbolic one, GIT_REFCOUNT_DEC(db) when attached (db may be NULL for a sys/refs.h allocation), then git__free of the struct. NULL is a no-op. Needs no repository: the refdb outlives it through the counted db.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Clears the object/attr/submodule caches, frees the grafts (NULL afterwards, never reloaded: later commit parses call git_grafts_get(NULL) -> GIT_ASSERT_ARG -1, ignoring grafts and leaving an 'invalid argument' error) and drops the repo's refs to config/index/odb/refdb (disowning them; counted refs handed out stay valid). Always 0. Wrapper: RepositoryMut::cleanup (exclusive, so no borrowed result is live).

GIT_ASSERT_ARG (aborts in the Debug/coverage build). Overwritten without releasing what it held (count = 0, commits = NULL first), so a wrapper must clear a reused CommitArray first (CommitArrayMut::clear). On success: the HEAD commit then each MERGE_HEAD commit, as git_commit_lookup references in a git_vector_detach'd libgit2 buffer the caller owns (git_commitarray_dispose). {NULL, 0} for an unborn HEAD (returns 0) and on failure. C DEFECT: on a failure after the first parent is collected (malformed MERGE_HEAD line: 'unable to parse OID - invalid length'; or a MERGE_HEAD id that is not a commit, which insert_mergehead turns into -1), done: frees the collected commits with git__free instead of git_commit_free while the repository's object cache still holds them: the next lookup of that commit, or the cache teardown in git_repository_free, is a heap-use-after-free (ASan-confirmed, repository wave 0 batch 2). The safe wrapper must not reach it (e.g. pre-validate MERGE_HEAD, or rebuild the routine over revparse + mergehead_foreach in Rust). Further C defects (repository wave 1 batch 2): HEAD resolving to a non-commit is put in the array as a commit (a tag object, or a blob/tree, read later through git_commit_* as the wrong struct); and git_revparse_ext leaks HEAD's reference when HEAD names a missing or unreadable object (revparse_lookup_object drops `ref` when git_object_lookup fails; LSan). The Rust RepositoryRef::commit_parents is a composition (Replaces anchor): git_reference_dwim("HEAD") + git_object_lookup(ANY) (freeing the reference on every path), git_object_peel to COMMIT (tags peel, others GIT_EINVALIDSPEC), git_repository_mergehead_foreach + git_commit_lookup into a Rust Vec released by git_commit_free on error, and an OdbDataVec buffer adopted by CommitArray::from_raw.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Read (revparse HEAD, MERGE_HEAD) and its object cache updated by the lookups; not retained by the result: the commits outlive the repository.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL(NULL); only read.
repo->commondir, set at open and freed only by git_repository_free; NULL for git_repository_new (in-memory). Borrowed for the repository's life (RepositoryRef<'a> -> Option<&'a CStr>).

Receives an up-ref'd (GIT_REFCOUNT_INC) reference to the repository's lazily loaded config (repo->_config, owner = repo), released by git_config_free: a SHARED reference (ConfigArc), since the repository holds and writes through another. On a load failure __weakptr still writes *out = repo->_config, i.e. NULL, and -1 is returned before the up-ref. The config outlives the repository (git_repository_free disowns it before its own down-ref).
Not asserted (dereferenced unconditionally). Its config slot is set with a compare-and-swap on first load.

Out slot: NULLed by git_config_snapshot, then a fresh git_config_new config (count 1, no owner) holding snapshots of the repo config's backends: the caller's sole reference (ConfigBox), released by git_config_free. Untouched if the repo config itself fails to load (returns that error first).
Loads and caches repo->_config (weak) through the shared pointer; not retained by the snapshot.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Looks up HEAD, resolves it (git_repository_head: EUNBORNBRANCH for a missing branch), looks the target up as a COMMIT (so a HEAD detached at a tag FAILS, contrary to the header's 'peeled'), and rewrites HEAD with a reflog entry (signature from repo ident/config + git_signature_now: glibc tzset, which TSan reports across threads). 0 or error; HEAD untouched on failure.
NULL = empty; ':'-separated absolute paths; read for the call.

git_buf filled by git_buf_fromstr WITHOUT git_buf_tostr's sanitize: a reused reserved>0 allocation is overwritten and leaked, so the wrapper fills a fresh Buf::new(). Result: the gitdir with a trailing '/'. Untouched on failure.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call. A missing or unresolvable start ("" included) fails ENOTFOUND.

ref_name: sole invoker git_repository_fetchhead_foreach passes git_str_cstr of a per-line buffer reused for the next line (refs/heads/<n>, refs/tags/<n>, or a quoted name), or NULL when the line names none. Valid for the call only.
remote_url: points into the file buffer freed after the iteration; NULL for an old-format line (an id alone). Valid for the call only.
The entry's id, a stack git_oid of the repository's type; never NULL. Valid for the call only.

Caller's payload passed through untouched. Non-zero returns stop the iteration and are returned by foreach (git_error_set_after_callback names the callback only when no error is set). Single contract (one invoker): Rust FetchheadForeachCallback (closure; GIT_EUSER on Break or caught panic).
Released: cleanup drops the counted odb/refdb/config/index references, then every owned string, cache and array, then the struct (git__free). NULL is a no-op.
Only read (no assert: NULL crashes).

repo->namespace: set by open (FROM_ENV GIT_NAMESPACE) and replaced/freed by git_repository_set_namespace (git__free then strdup) and git_repository_free. Borrowed until the next set_namespace: that wrapper must take RepositoryMut.
NULL: derive from path when under the workdir, else no filters; "": no filters.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; written only on success, an id of repo->oid_type.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; relative paths join the workdir.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; workdir (NULL for bare/in-memory: a relative path is then taken from the cwd), oid_type, filter/attr caches.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG(head_out). On success a fresh reference (HEAD itself when direct, else the resolved branch) attached to repo's refdb, whose db->repo is uncounted: the wrapper returns ReferenceBox<'r> tied to the repo borrow. Untouched on failure: EUNBORNBRANCH (missing branch), ENOTFOUND (no HEAD, or in-memory repo).
Refdb loaded through the shared pointer.
Loads odb (in-memory repo: -1 'path cannot exist in repository') and HEAD; 1 only when HEAD is direct AND git_odb_exists(target) - a HEAD at a missing object reads as 0. -1 collapses every error.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Through git_repository_head_for_worktree: NULL commondir (in-memory repo) is strlen(NULL) in git_worktree_lookup. C DEFECT: tests the type of the FULLY RESOLVED reference, which is always direct, so an attached worktree HEAD answers 1. Rust replaces it: head_for_worktree's result is named "HEAD" exactly when HEAD is direct.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; joined to <commondir>/worktrees/<name>, never retained.

NULLed first. On success a resolved (direct) reference read through a repository opened for the worktree (git_repository_open_from_worktree) which is FREED before returning: its db->repo dangles (ASan-confirmed UAF via git_reference_owner/git_repository_path). Only name/target/peel/type and git_reference_free are safe: the wrapper copies it into an UnattachedReference (git_reference__alloc) and frees the original. ENOTFOUND for a missing worktree (stale error message) or unborn worktree branch.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; only read. commondir NULL (git_repository_new) -> git_worktree_lookup strlen(NULL): SIGSEGV/UBSan nonnull; the wrapper refuses first (ENOTFOUND, GIT_ERROR_WORKTREE).
git_repository_head then clears the error on EUNBORNBRANCH -> 1; any other error collapses to -1.
As name, for repo->ident_email. (The slot itself is written; mutable=false for the const char pointee.)

Out slot (no assert) receiving repo->ident_name: NULL or the repo's own string, replaced (atomic swap, then freed) by git_repository_set_ident and freed by git_repository_free; borrowed until then (set_ident wrapper must take RepositoryMut). (The slot itself is written; mutable=false for the const char pointee.)
Only read; always returns 0.

On success one more counted reference (GIT_REFCOUNT_INC) to repo->_index (rc.owner = repo, uncounted, cleared when the repo releases it): IndexArc. On failure *out may hold the repo's own (uncounted for the caller) pointer or NULL, returns -1 whatever the cause (in-memory repo: 'path cannot exist in repository'). Must not be adopted on failure.
Index loaded and cached through the shared pointer.
Path read for the call only.

Out slot written by the inner git_repository_open; init_ext may fail AFTER that open (refdb init, origin creation) leaving a live repository in *out that the caller must free. Not NULLed first: callers must pre-NULL it.
Path read for the call only.
Options; init_ext WRITES opts->flags (|= GIT_REPOSITORY_INIT__IS_REINIT on reinit), otherwise read for the call.
As git_repository_init: *out may hold a live repository even when the call fails after the inner open; never NULLed first.

Caller storage (usually a stack local) overwritten whole with GIT_REPOSITORY_INIT_OPTIONS_INIT (memcpy) after the version check; no NULL check, so NULL crashes. Version != 1 returns -1 with GIT_ERROR_INVALID and leaves the storage untouched. No allocation, no global state.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; only read; 0/1.

HEAD lookup error returned as is (ENOTFOUND when missing); otherwise symbolic HEAD == init.defaultBranch (or master) && no reference; repo_contains_no_reference's negative error is truthy in the && chain (reads as empty).
lstat <commondir>/shallow: 1 when non-empty, 0 when missing/empty; commondir NULL (in-memory) joins to plain 'shallow' in the process cwd.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; only read; 0/1.
git_buf via GIT_BUF_WRAP_PRIVATE (sanitize, reuse, tostr): fill a fresh Buf::new().
Only read. The item indexes items[] unchecked: GIT_REPOSITORY_ITEM__LAST and above read out of bounds; the wrapper takes the Item enum.
The one id parsed from a MERGE_HEAD line into a stack git_oid of git_repository_mergehead_foreach; lent for the call only, never retained or freed by the callback.
Caller's opaque payload, passed through unchanged by git_repository_mergehead_foreach (and commit_parents' insert_mergehead, a struct mergehead_data); never freed by libgit2.
git_buf out filled through GIT_BUF_WRAP_PRIVATE (sanitize, then git_buf_fromstr): a reserved>0 buffer is reused/reallocated, the result owned by the caller's struct (released with git_buf_dispose).
Reads repo->gitdir only. A repository without one (git_repository_new / wrap_odb) joins NULL+"MERGE_MSG" and reads ./MERGE_MSG relative to the cwd (probed).
Reads repo->gitdir and unlinks <gitdir>/MERGE_MSG; the struct is not written. p_unlink failure returns -1 with no libgit2 error set; a pathless repository unlinks ./MERGE_MSG in the cwd (probed).
Out slot; written with a fresh bare repository (no paths, no backends) or left as repository_alloc's NULL on OOM.
Options read for the call only (version, oid_type); NULL means defaults.
Out slot; *out = repository_alloc() is written before the allocation check, so NULL on failure. GIT_ASSERT_ARG on an invalid non-zero opts->oid_type.

Caller storage (usually a stack local) overwritten whole with GIT_REPOSITORY_NEW_OPTIONS_INIT (memcpy) after GIT_ASSERT_ARG(opts) and the version check. Version != 1 returns -1 with GIT_ERROR_INVALID and leaves the storage untouched. No allocation, no global state.

Out slot: one new counted reference (GIT_REFCOUNT_INC) to the repository's odb, lazily created and owned (rc.owner = repo) by it; released with git_odb_free. Left untouched on failure (-1). The odb reads the owner's object cache through rc.owner, so the reference must not outlive the repository.
Lazily creates and atomically installs repo->_odb (a cache fill through a shared pointer).
Reads repo->oid_type; NULL returns 0 (no type).
Path read for the call only.
Out slot; open_ext NULLs it first, writes the repository only on success (frees it on failure).
Path read for the call only (git_fs_path_prettify_dir).

Out slot; written ONLY on success and not NULLed first. Defect: when read_repository_format fails (unsupported repositoryformatversion, unknown extension/objectformat) the allocated repository and its gitdir/commondir strings leak, and an allocation failure after repository_alloc leaks too.
Ceiling dirs list read for the call; NULL = none.
Out slot, may be NULL (probe only). NULLed first; written only on success; the half-built repository is freed on failure.
Start path read for the call; NULL only valid with GIT_REPOSITORY_OPEN_FROM_ENV.
Out slot NULLed first, written with a fresh repository (git_repository_open of the gitlink path less '.git') the caller owns and frees with git_repository_free.
Only wt->gitlink_path is read; the opened repository keeps no pointer into the worktree. A gitlink path not ending in '.git' (case-insensitive) returns -1 without setting an error.
Reads repo->gitdir; GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL(repo, NULL).
repo->gitdir, owned by the repository and freed with it; assigned only by the open routines, never replaced afterwards. NULL for a repository without a git directory (git_repository_new, wrap_odb).

Out slot: one new counted reference to the repository's refdb (lazily opened, rc.owner = repo); released with git_refdb_free. The refdb and its backend keep an uncounted pointer to the repository (db->repo), so the reference must not outlive it. Untouched on failure (-1).
Lazily opens and installs repo->_refdb (cache fill).

Rewrites the repository's config file (core.* fs probes) at <gitdir>/config, clears the configmap cache, and with recurse reinitialises submodules (errors ignored). A pathless repository writes ./config in the cwd (probed).
Writes core.bare/core.worktree through the repo config, frees repo->workdir and sets is_bare; a no-op returning 0 when already bare.
Retained: GIT_REFCOUNT_INC + rc.owner = repo; the caller keeps its own reference. GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL. A sole caller reference stops being sole.
Swaps repo->_config: the old one is disowned (OWN NULL) and released.
Reference name read for the call (GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL); copied into the new HEAD.
Reads/writes HEAD and the reflog through the repository's refdb (lazily opened); the struct itself only gets cache fills.
Id read for the call (GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL). Looked up with git_object_lookup: an id of another type than the repository's overflows the loose path buffer (SHA256 id in SHA1 repo).
As set_head; also looks the id up through the object db (cache fill).
Read for the call: its id and description (the reflog's target name). GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL. Same id-type hazard as set_head_detached when the commit comes from a repository of another type.
As set_head_detached.
Copied with git__strdup; NULL clears.
Copied with git__strdup; NULL clears. On an email strdup failure the name copy leaks.
Atomically swaps ident_name/ident_email and frees the previous strings (which git_repository_ident lent).
Retained when non-NULL: GIT_REFCOUNT_INC + rc.owner = repo (caller keeps its reference). NULL removes the repository's index.
Swaps repo->_index: the old one is disowned and released.
Copied with git__strdup; NULL clears the namespace.
Frees repo->namespace (which git_repository_get_namespace lent) and stores a copy; no NULL check on repo. On strdup failure namespace is left NULL and -1 returned.
Retained: GIT_REFCOUNT_INC + rc.owner = repo, overwriting any previous owner silently (the first owner's lookups then use the new owner's cache). GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL.
Swaps repo->_odb: the old one is disowned and released.

Retained: GIT_REFCOUNT_INC + rc.owner = repo. db->repo (the repository it was opened for) is NOT updated: the installing repository then dereferences that repository on every ref operation, so it must outlive them. GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL.
Swaps repo->_refdb: the old one is disowned and released.

Frees and replaces repo->workdir, clears is_bare; with update_gitlink writes <workdir>/.git and core.worktree/core.bare through the config. A pathless repository with update_gitlink dereferences NULL (git__suffixcmp(NULL), probed SIGSEGV).
Path read for the call (prettified copy stored); GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL.

Probes marker files under repo->gitdir and looks REVERT_HEAD/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD up through the refdb (cache fill). A pathless repository hits GIT_ASSERT_ARG(string) in git_str_puts: -1 in release, abort in Debug.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Removes MERGE_HEAD/MERGE_MODE/MERGE_MSG/BISECT_LOG (p_unlink: fails -1 WITHOUT an error message) and rebase-merge/, rebase-apply/, sequencer/ (rmdir_r) joined to repo->gitdir, then REVERT_HEAD/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD through the refdb (lazily loaded into the repo). HAZARD: with a NULL gitdir (git_repository_new / wrap_odb) git_str_joinpath treats NULL as "" and the files backend uses NULL paths too, so it removes those names relative to the process's cwd; the safe wrapper refuses such a repository (ENOTFOUND, 'path cannot exist in repository'). Wrapped on RepositoryMut.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. git_submodule_cache_init(&repo->submodule_cache, repo) OVERWRITES the slot without freeing a previous cache: a second call leaks the old cache and its submodule references (LSan-confirmed); on failure the slot keeps its old value. git_submodule_lookup and diff generation read the slot (diff keeps it in a local across notify callbacks), so the wrapper takes RepositoryMut and clears first.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. git_submodule_cache_free(repo->submodule_cache) (NULL no-op; drops each cached submodule's reference, then the map and struct) and NULLs the slot; always returns 0. Also run by git_repository__cleanup / free. Submodules looked up through the cache hold their own reference and survive.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL(NULL); reads is_bare and workdir only.

repo->workdir (with trailing slash), or NULL for a bare repository or one without paths. Owned by the repository; freed/replaced only by git_repository_set_workdir and git_repository_set_bare (and git_repository_free), so it borrows the repository until such a call: the Rust getter ties it to RepositoryRef<'a>, which requires those setters to take RepositoryMut.

Not asserted (odb->options.oid_type read first; GIT_ASSERT on an invalid type, leaking the repo). git_repository_set_odb takes its own counted reference (GIT_REFCOUNT_INC) and makes the repository the odb's owner (rc.owner) without checking for a previous owner; the caller keeps its reference. So the wrapper accepts only an odb no repository owns (OdbArc<'static>) and releases the caller's reference after the call.

Out slot, not asserted and not NULLed: written only on success with a fresh repository (no paths, is_bare 0, refdb_type FILES) owned by the caller (git_repository_free); left untouched when repository_alloc fails.
Out slot: written only on success with a git_signature_now result owned by the caller.
The repository whose config snapshot supplies user.name / user.email; only used for the call.

Optional out slot: NULL is accepted (GIT_ASSERT_ARG(author_out || committer_out) only refuses both NULL), in which case no author is built. Written only on success with a fresh git_signature_new result owned by the caller (git_signature_free). On error both temporaries are released with git__free, leaking their strings; a NULL author_out leaves the slot untouched.
Optional out slot, as author_out, from the GIT_COMMITTER_* variables.
The repository whose config snapshot supplies user.name / user.email; only used for the call.

Out slot, written only on success with a fresh git__calloc'd copy owned by the caller (git_signature_free). Left untouched when source is NULL (returns 0) or an allocation fails (returns -1, leaking the partial copy and any string already duplicated).

Only read: name and email are git__strdup'd (strdup(NULL) crashes, so a signature whose parse lost a string to OOM cannot be copied), when copied field by field. NULL source returns 0 without writing dest (blame's dup_hunk relies on it).

NULL is a no-op. Frees name and email with git__free (either may be NULL after an allocation failure in git_signature__parse), NULLs them, then frees the struct with git__free. Every public owned signature (new/now/default/default_from_env/from_buffer/dup) is released here; commits, tags, notes, reflog entries and blame hunks call it on the signatures they own. Pool copies (git_signature__pdup) must never reach it.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; the whole NUL-terminated signature line `Name <email> secs zone`, read for the call and never retained.

Out slot, NULLed first: on success a fresh git__calloc'd signature owned by the caller (git_signature_free). Its name or email is NULL when the unchecked extract_trimmed allocation failed, yet 0 is returned. On a parse error (GIT_EINVALID) the struct is freed and out stays NULL.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call and copied (trimmed) into fresh libgit2-allocated strings, never retained.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call and copied (trimmed) into fresh libgit2-allocated strings, never retained.

Out slot, set to NULL once the arguments pass their asserts: receives a fresh git__calloc'd signature with trimmed git__substrdup copies of name and email (sign derived from the offset), owned by the caller (git_signature_free). Stays NULL on failure (angle brackets, empty trimmed name/email, OOM); an allocation failure for a string leaks the half-built signature.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call and copied (trimmed) into fresh libgit2-allocated strings, never retained.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call and copied (trimmed) into fresh libgit2-allocated strings, never retained.
Out slot; as git_signature_new, with the current time and local UTC offset (time(), gmtime_r, mktime).

Caller storage filled in place: sets all three members to the stdalloc malloc/realloc/free forwarders and returns 0. Not exported from libgit2.so (declared in git2/sys/alloc.h without GIT_EXTERN, hidden), so it cannot be bound; git_allocator_global_init applies it to git__allocator.

Read only. NULL elements of src->strings are skipped silently, so the copy's count can be smaller than src->count (with spare calloc'd slots). Declared only in deprecated.h and compiled hidden under GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD: not in libgit2.so's dynamic symbols, so Rust copies go through OdbDataStrVec::dup_all instead (same order: array first, then each string; a failure releases the partial copy).

Caller storage, memset to zero first (not disposed: anything it held leaks), then filled with a git__calloc'd array of git__strdup copies; on a failed strdup the partial copy is disposed and `tgt` re-zeroed. GIT_ASSERT_ARG on NULL.

The caller's struct, borrowed for the call (libgit2 never allocates a git_strarray). NULL returns. Frees strings[0..count) and then `strings` with git__free, then memsets the struct to zero, leaving it reusable. Requires the struct to own its array and strings (the OUTPUT contract of git_strarray.strings); a NULL `strings` with count > 0 derefs NULL. With NULL `strings` and count 0 it still calls git__free(NULL), which reads git__allocator unsynchronised against a concurrent first git_libgit2_init, so the Rust policy skips C for that empty state.

Sole invoker git_trace__write_fmt (src/libgit2/trace.h, via git_trace) passes git_str_cstr of a local git_str it formats the message into and disposes right after the call: borrowed for the call only, never NULL (an allocated string, or the static git_str__initstr / git_str__oom sentinel after a failed vprintf), NUL-terminated, arbitrary bytes (server responses are traced verbatim, so not necessarily UTF-8). git_trace call sites: transports/httpclient.c (DEBUG 'Connecting to remote/proxy', 'Sending ... request'; TRACE 'Received:' and the request dump) in every build, and streams/stransport.c:269 (INFO, an SSLRead error) only under GIT_HTTPS_SECURETRANSPORT, out of the campaign's scope. The level argument is always a named GIT_TRACE_* constant at every call site (INFO/DEBUG/TRACE in practice; never NONE). Called on whichever thread runs the traced libgit2 call, concurrently from several threads; the callback reads no payload (none exists), and git_trace__data is read without a lock.

Function pointer stored verbatim in the unlocked global git_trace__data.callback and called (by git_trace, from any thread running the HTTP client) until the next git_trace_set: borrowed for as long as it stays installed, never released. NULL only with level == 0 (GIT_ASSERT_ARG: -1 GIT_ERROR_INVALID in release, abort in debug). git_trace reads level/callback without a lock and re-reads callback after the NULL check (TOCTOU), so a set racing a trace is a data race and clearing can make C call NULL.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG, then set to NULL; receives the worktree git_worktree_lookup loads once the gitdir, working directory, refs and checkout are created, owned by the caller (git_worktree_free). Stays NULL on failure.

Caller-provided storage, written in full by memcpy of GIT_WORKTREE_ADD_OPTIONS_INIT ({1, 0, 0, NULL, GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_INIT}) when version is in 1..=GIT_WORKTREE_ADD_OPTIONS_VERSION; left untouched (error set, -1) otherwise. No NULL check: a NULL opts with a valid version is a NULL write. Reaches no allocator on success.

NULL is a no-op. Frees commondir_path, worktree_path, gitlink_path, gitdir_path, parent_path and name with git__free, then the struct. Releases every worktree the constructors hand out; also open_worktree_dir's error path, get_url_base, git_repository_foreach_worktree and git_repository_head_for_worktree on the worktrees they looked up.

Optional out buffer: NULL skips reading the reason. Otherwise converted with git_buf_tostr (takes over an owned buffer), cleared, filled with the `locked` file's contents when locked, and handed back with git_buf_fromstr (owned when allocated; static empty string when not locked). Caller disposes with git_buf_dispose. On a read error (e.g. `locked` is a directory) the buffer is left as converted.
Live worktree, only read (its six owned strings); never retained. Reads the file system (<gitdir>/locked), not wt->locked.

Read-only despite the non-const type: GIT_ERROR_CHECK_VERSION reads version (NULL passes), then memcpy copies it into a local; NULL means the {VERSION, 0} defaults. Not retained past the call. Flag bits outside git_worktree_prune_t are ignored.

Live worktree, only read (its six owned strings); never retained. Not asserted. Returns 1 prunable, 0 not (the reason set as the thread's error), <0 on a version or locked-read error. Precedence slip `ret = (git_str_printf(..) < 0)` makes an OOM there return 1.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; reads repo->commondir only. HAZARD: NULL commondir (repository without paths) joins as "", listing <cwd>/worktrees/; the wrapper returns an empty list instead.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Overwritten with {NULL,0} first, without disposing what it held; on success receives a git_vector_detach'd array of git__strdup'd names owned by the caller (git_strarray_dispose); NULL/0 when worktrees/ is missing or empty. C DEFECT: entries failing is_worktree_dir are removed with git_vector_remove inside git_vector_foreach, so the entry after each removed one is never checked and is listed (C-confirmed: 4 junk dirs + 1 worktree lists a junk name). A dirload failure leaks the partial vector.
Optional lock reason, attached not-owned and written to the file; read for the call only. NULL = empty file.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Live worktree, WRITTEN: sets wt->locked = 1 after creating <gitdir>/locked (O_EXCL). Returns GIT_ELOCKED WITHOUT setting an error when already locked. Wrapped on WorktreeMut (the Worktree Sync proof relies on it).
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; joined into the worktree's gitdir path and git__strdup'd as its name, never retained.

Out slot, set to NULL after the asserts on repo and name (out itself is not asserted); receives a fresh git__calloc'd worktree whose strings are all copies, owned by the caller (git_worktree_free). Stays NULL on failure: GIT_ENOTFOUND when `<commondir>/worktrees/<name>` is not a directory, -1 when it lacks commondir/gitdir/HEAD or a link cannot be read.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call (commondir, workdir), never retained: the worktree copies what it needs, so it may outlive the repository. HAZARD: repo->commondir goes to strlen through git_str_join3 unchecked, so a repository without paths (git_repository_new, wrap_odb: commondir NULL) is a NULL dereference; the wrapper refuses it first. Failures with no error message: GIT_ENOTFOUND (no such dir) and -1 (not a worktree dir).
GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL(NULL); reads wt->name.
wt->name, a non-NULL git__strdup'd copy the worktree owns; freed only by git_worktree_free, so it borrows the worktree.

Out slot, NOT reset on failure (left as the caller initialised it); receives a fresh worktree owned by the caller (git_worktree_free) when repo is a worktree's repository. Fails with GIT_ERROR_WORKTREE 'cannot open worktree of a non-worktree repo' otherwise.
Not asserted: NULL dereferences in git_repository_is_worktree. Read for the call (gitdir, commondir), never retained.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL(NULL); reads wt->worktree_path.
wt->worktree_path, dirname of the gitdir link: a non-NULL copy the worktree owns, freed only by git_worktree_free, so it borrows the worktree.

Read-only despite the non-const type: GIT_ERROR_CHECK_VERSION reads version (NULL passes), then memcpy copies it into a local; NULL means the {VERSION, 0} defaults. Not retained past the call. Flag bits outside git_worktree_prune_t are ignored. HAZARD for the safe wrapper: prune tests `!git_worktree_is_prunable(wt, &popts)`, so an is_prunable ERROR (<0, e.g. GIT_ENOTFOUND 'requested file is a directory' when the `locked` entry cannot be read, checked only without GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_LOCKED) counts as prunable and prune deletes the gitdir anyway; git_futils_rmdir_r then clears the error state (pinned in tests/equiv/worktree.rs::prune_options::prune_reads_the_options_alike).

Live worktree, only read (its six owned strings); never retained. Not asserted. Deletes <commondir>/worktrees/<name> and, with PRUNE_WORKING_TREE, dirname(gitlink_path) on disk; the struct stays valid. Treats an is_prunable error as prunable (see opts); the safe wrapper calls is_prunable first and reports its error.

Caller-provided storage, written in full by memcpy of the {VERSION, 0} template when version is in 1..=GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_OPTIONS_VERSION; left untouched (error set) otherwise. GIT_INIT_STRUCTURE_FROM_TEMPLATE has no NULL check: a NULL opts with a valid version is a NULL write.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Live worktree, WRITTEN: clears wt->locked after unlinking <gitdir>/locked. Returns 1 when not locked; a failed p_unlink (e.g. `locked` is a directory) returns -1 WITHOUT setting an error. Wrapped on WorktreeMut.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Live worktree, only read (its six owned strings); never retained. Checks gitdir_path (is_worktree_dir), parent_path (when set), commondir_path, worktree_path exist; GIT_ERROR + GIT_ERROR_WORKTREE message on the first missing.
